with the indication of the letter of origin

After each thought is indicated, in grey italics, the letter of Mother Rosa Gattorno from which it is taken (number, addressee, place and date, according to the edition of the Letters). “Cf.” indicates only a partial correspondence, to be checked against the text; the thoughts without any indication have not been traced.

THREADS OF GOLD

MAXIMS, THOUGHTS DRAWN FROM THE LETTERS WHICH THE SERVANT OF GOD ROSA GATTORNO WROTE TO THE FIRST DAUGHTERS OF SAINT ANNE

IN REMEMBRANCE OF THE FIRST FIFTIETH ANNIVERSARY OF THE FOUNDATION MDCCCLXVI-MCMXVI

IMPRIMATUR

Fr. Albertus Lepidi O. P. S. P. Ap. Magister.

IMPRIMATUR

Franciscus Faberi, Vic. Urbis Adsessor.

Rome - Tip. Agostiniana

TO YOU

VENERATED MOTHER FOUNDRESS

ROSA GATTORNO

MAY THIS FIRST HUMBLE FLOWER

FRAGRANT WITH YOUR VIRTUES

ON THE 50th ANNIVERSARY OF THE FOUNDATION

OF OUR INSTITUTE

* * *

TELL YOU HOW MUCH

YOUR DAUGHTERS LOVE YOU

AND HOW IN THE “SPIRIT” WHICH YOU INFUSED INTO THEM

THEY WILL LIVE WITH ONE HEART

TO HAND IT DOWN INTACT TO THE MORROW

OF THIS WORK OF GOD

THAT IT MAY REMAIN STRONG AND PURE

AS YOU LEFT IT TO US

Mother Celsa Speranza implores the Apostolic blessing of His Holiness Benedict XV upon the “gift” to be offered to the “Daughters of Saint Anne” on the occasion of the first 50th anniversary of the foundation of the Institute.

Most Holy Father,

The Superior General of the “Daughters of Saint Anne”, Mother Celsa Speranza, prostrate to kiss the Holy Feet, in the name also of her Council, sets forth to Your Holiness that, on the occasion of the first fiftieth anniversary of the foundation of the Institute, which will be celebrated on the day of the Immaculate Conception of this present year 1916, she would wish to give in remembrance to the “Daughters of Saint Anne” a Collection of thoughts and counsels of the venerated Foundress ROSA GATTORNO. So that the gift may bring greater spiritual profit to the souls of the dear daughters, she begs Your Holiness to deign to grant this Collection and this pious intention your sovereign, comforting, Fatherly approval and a special Apostolic blessing.

And for the grace, etc.

Rome, 10 April 1916.

The Holy Father Benedict XV deigned to reply with the following autograph:

To the Rev. Mother

Celsa Speranza

Superior General of the “Daughters of Saint Anne”

The fiftieth anniversary of existence which the Institute of the “Daughters of Saint Anne” is preparing to celebrate on the coming feast of Mary Immaculate calls Us to consider the consoling growth which the worthy Sodality has attained in so short a period, not only in Italy, but also in the most remote regions.

And since it is lawful to judge the tree by its fruits, We think We may affirm that the young Institute has visibly borne with it the blessing of God.

This wide and rapid progress along a road which always, but especially at its beginnings, is strewn with obstacles, cannot but be traced back to the goodness of the spirit which animated the Mother Foundress, and which she poured into her pupils.

We therefore deem worthy of praise the pious resolve of the present Superior General to gather and spread among the Sisters, as a fitting remembrance of the happy anniversary, a florilegium of the most notable thoughts and counsels which Mother Rosa Gattorno went on scattering in her mystical letters, and which reflect that spirit.

Threads of Gold truly are those thoughts and those counsels; and while they are the treasuries of golden virtue, they inspire a virtue equally golden in her faithful disciples, and bind the daughters of Saint Anne to Mother Gattorno with the noble and holy bonds of love, of gratitude, of imitation.

Applauding therefore this wholesome initiative, We offer Our good wishes to these good Religious, desiring for them that, link by link, the chain of the Mother and of the Daughters may be unbroken and of the choicest gold; and that each may show forth in her works the spirit and the image of the Mother Foundress, rendering full, lasting and fruitful the most ample graces which We invoke upon each one, imparting to them with a fatherly heart the Apostolic blessing.

From the Vatican

on Low Sunday (Dominica in Albis) of the year 1916

Beloved dear daughters,

The fiftieth anniversary of the Foundation of our Institute is for me a welcome occasion to offer you a gift which will be most dear to you, because it will let you hear once more the wise and loving voice of the venerated Mother Foundress, of Her whom rightly and with filial tenderness we call Mother Rosa, of Her who was our first Mistress in holy and generous things, and who is our surest support, our most effective comfort after God and Mother Saint Anne, in all the difficult moments of our life of labour and sacrifice.

And this gift your poor Mother Celsa offers you under the title of Threads of Gold, a title which at once explains to you that it is a collection of slight and simple things, but valuable and precious. I have gleaned them here and there while putting in order the surviving letters of the first heroic “daughters”, now deceased, in the period which runs from the foundation in 1866 to 1879; they are judgements, counsels, teachings which our venerated Foundress wrote to them in order to form them according to the spirit of the Institute and according to the Heart of God.

The Threads of Gold are, so to speak, the essence of the love, of the wisdom, of the virtues with which our Foundress was adorned; they are the fruit of an experience often made of cross and martyrdom; and they will serve to show you the true way of God, and to guide you, like a ray of light, to the pure source of good, of hope and above all of that heroic love made of strong and upright works.

In offering them to you I press you affectionately to my heart, to bear witness to the tenderness I have for you, and to the great love I feel for this Work of God built by that venerated Mother Rosa of ours upon a heap of crosses, and cemented with so many tears, with so much penance; in offering them to you I say to you aloud: “Dear daughters, courage; let us show ourselves, and let us truly be, worthy of our recent and yet glorious past: glorious for sufferings, poverty, struggles and triumphs; glorious for heroic deeds of charity, of sacrifice, of generosity; glorious for so many virtues, common and personal, which I am pleased to leave in the shadow where they were born, and from where they will shine forth in due time.

Now, in celebrating the fiftieth anniversary of the Foundation, let us temper our strength so as to go forward with courage. Our “Venerated Mother Rosa” left us strongly united in one heart alone: may the Threads of Gold renew and strengthen these holy bonds, so as to leave intact for the morrow of the Institute that spirit which She laboured to infuse during thirty-four years of government: a spirit not of greatness, of comfort, of gain, of ambition; but of labour, of sacrifice, of generosity, of modesty, and above all of that disinterested charity quickened by the sacred fire of the love of God and by prayer.

This, this, dear daughters, strengthen mightily today. God asks it of you, Mother Rosa wills it, the Threads of Gold will be flashes of light for you. Every day read, meditate on a thought, a counsel, a teaching; nourish your soul with this wholesome food, so that it may become the strength of your strength, the soul of your actions, the honour of our Holy Habit. Read, read again, meditate every day on some page, and you will feel how much the venerated Mother Rosa loved you and loves you, and by what way she wants you to be worthy and holy “Daughters of Saint Anne”. For us, for those who will come after us, She gave teachings while teaching her own “daughters”.

May the gift of this your poor Mother Celsa therefore be dear to you: and may it serve to strengthen and to adorn the “thread of gold” of the motherly love with which she presses you all to her heart, to infuse into you a lofty, invincible love for the Institute, for its traditions, for its Rules, for its spirit, so that you may cooperate, united in one heart alone, in the complete fulfilment of the future which the holy Pontiff Pius IX, of holy memory, summed up in his first prophetic blessing of the Work in January 1866, when, encouraging the Venerated Mother to the foundation, he said to her:

“Your Institute, O Rosa, will spread rapidly throughout the whole world like the flight of the dove, and will last until the end of the ages”.

Rome, April 1916.

DEAR daughter, I have not a moment’s time; I find no rest either by night or by day. May the will of dear Jesus always be done.

cf. Letter 11, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 23 April 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

My daughters, I hope that Jesus will have inspired in the hearts of all of you new and ever-living resolutions of love and of constancy in wishing to follow Him; and certainly you will put them into practice.

cf. Letter 11, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 23 April 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

My beloved daughters, may God bless you all; I do not cease and never will cease to offer prayers for you, that God may make you saints, and great saints.

cf. Letter 23, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 August 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

… My health is in a very bad state (you will have heard it from your sister - certainly I should never have written it to you). As long as I believed I was dying, I remembered you, and I felt sorrow at leaving you without seeing you! And then, how I was leaving you!… But the good God preserved me, and I hope that I will leave you well settled before I die.

cf. Letter 26, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 4 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, open your heart to me with all frankness, as does with you this most poor mother, who once again feels unwell, and is greatly oppressed by the burdens of this poor house!

cf. Letter 29, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 19 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, believe that this poor mother of yours always keeps you present… Be of good heart, and believe that soon you will be consoled.

cf. Letter 37, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 3 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughters, I assure you that this poor mother of yours has nothing else in her mind but your holiness, and, unworthy as she is, she never ceases to raise prayers to the Most High for your spiritual and temporal welfare.

Letter 128, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 6 June 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, I assure you that this poor Mother of yours shares in your afflictions; but she would wish you to be my imitator in courage and in confidence in God, the sole object of our works, because for Him alone we do everything, and from Him alone we want our wages; never from men.

cf. Letter 132, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 July 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

In the midst of the tumult of the world, where nothing reigns but sin, I count it an honour to be in the last little corner of the scullery in our house. My God! what a hell (in the world). Dear Daughter of Saint Anne, bless aloud the Lord who from an abyss brought you to the delightful heights of His Dwelling.

cf. Letter 142, to Carolina Pezzoni, Genova, 25 August 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, be at peace and continue to believe that this poor Mother of yours always keeps you close: in the morning, in the chapel at meditation, at Communion, everywhere!

cf. Letter 148, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 27 September 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

I see that you are in a not very cheerful mood: why, my daughter? Courage; you wish to follow your poor mother, and do you not know what her road is, full of the sharpest thorns? If then you know that I always keep you with me, you must needs suffer.

cf. Letter 160, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 22 November 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

(For certain souls): Jesus remains always on the Cross, because they do not want to stay there; nor even to carry it: they leave it all upon His Most Holy Shoulders. So I have thought of having it given to me, and of obtaining Tabor for them, so that - by dint of little sweets - they may become His true disciples, and one day I may have them all for an eternity at my side, in Paradise, through the Merits of our Bridegroom Jesus; for were it not for Him, my God! where would this unhappy woman be, because of her sins?

Letter 167, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 December 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

My God! to You I entrust these souls whom You have entrusted to me: now I place them for all this time in the Heart of Your Son Jesus, and do You cover them with heavenly dew, so that they may be defended from every least encounter. In this retreat of the Heart of Jesus may they learn the true school of Your Divine Love.

Letter 57, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 25 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My God, bless them (my dear daughters) and strengthen them in suffering; pour upon them the choicest blessings.

Letter 57, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 25 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughters, I keep you always with me, and in a particular way the Superiors; and every day I commend them to God, that He may give them light to direct their community well.

cf. Letter 60, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Roma, 1 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

May God bless you all, and one day may that God who here on earth was so favourable to you be merciful to you in heaven.

Letter 60, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Roma, 1 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Believe me, dear daughters, the sin of idleness I do not have; perhaps the only one which, at the judgement seat of God, I will not find along with all the others: I have committed them all.

Letter 111, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 15 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Be at peace again, and think that this poor Mother of yours always holds you tight to herself, because she desires that the Holy Mother make you a saint; and she says to the Eternal Father: “Make of this soul a true kneading of Your will, so that in everything she may find pleasure in serving You, our Father, our support, our guide”.

Letter 115, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 17 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I am entirely equal towards all and I bear an entirely equal affection for all… Only, after having made every trial, and having suffered as much as is humanly possible, one must needs detach from one’s heart those souls for whom one sees that there is no other remedy.

cf. Letter 141, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 2 December 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I am poor in everything, and I do not know how you, my daughter, can have such attachment to this wretched Mother of yours, worthy to be abhorred by all: this is my portion.

cf. Letter 157, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Nizza, 27 January 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Our Eternal Father teaches me that one must also give tokens of goodwill to those who deserve them, just as we must use the lash when there is need.

cf. Letter 252, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Ferrara, 8 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

If it is true that you love me, take care of yourselves and keep yourselves well: the Work of the Lord has need of robust and healthy persons.

Letter 83, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Roma, 14 (March) April 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Try to take care of yourself and to become strong; otherwise you can never be fit to serve God.

* * *

Dear daughter, be cheerful, for your Mother wills it, and be always ready to receive from the hands of your Bridegroom His cross, so as to lighten His load a little. Yes, answer me that you will embrace your cross and give it a thousand kisses for me; I will say to Jesus: give my dear daughter the less heavy part, and the bigger one to me.

Letter 183, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 27 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, this poor Mother of yours always holds you tight to the Heart of Jesus, so that she may have you with her for an eternity of joy! This is my wealth, this is what I promise you; I think of giving you nothing else. Yes, my daughter, if you persevere in your vocation, you will have what I tell you: yes, I will it. So then, take heart, let us put into practice what with words we say to our dear Jesus.

cf. Letter 26, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 22 January 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

My good dear daughters, my Jesus sends word to you that you are the darlings of His Heart. Oh, dear daughters, woe to you if any one should make herself unworthy of it! what horror! no, no, I will not think of it; but I stay only with you in the Heart of my God, where I keep you, I hold you tight and I leave you - as a pledge - a thousand blessings, so that you may all become saints: may God do it, and I will it.

Letter 116, to the Sisters of the Hospital Community of Sampierdarena, Piacenza, 4 August 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Oh, my faraway dear daughters, does one perhaps think that she who has remained does not feel the emptiness?… certainly the Daughters who are in Italy do not cost me as many prayers as you… I can truly say it! You have left me your heart and your will: I am faithful, and always, every day, I offer it to God, and I hold you tight in the Heart of Jesus, and I pray my dear Crucified One not to let you run away, and to keep you always within Him. Oh! sweet dwelling, where nothing else is found but love and delight. You who desire to rejoice, keep yourselves held tight in Him, and in Him you will find love and delight: a love that gives every kind of sweetness!

Letter 299, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 21 May 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

Dear daughters, think of your Mother: it is true that I am poor and ugly, yet - I will say it to you again - I am your mother! Even poor little children, even if they have an ugly and poor mother, still love her, because she is their mamma, and they prefer her to a princess, and to all the nobles of the earth! I want to drive away the sad thought that afflicts me, namely that you (my faraway daughters) may not have your heart attached to your Mother!

cf. Letter 299, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 21 May 1879 — vol. 5

YOUR most poor Mother, full of affection for her dear daughter, every day holds her tight upon the Heart of her Bridegroom Jesus, to obtain for her from the precious wound a total absorption of herself and of every earthly thing of hers, so that she may come forth from it purified.

* * *

My God, steal the heart of my dear daughter, so that she may lose herself utterly in Your love, because she will never be able to find true love except in the centre of Your Heart. Saint Anne, make yourself the guardian of that Heart and enclose it in the breast of Jesus.

cf. Letter 6, to Caterina Rapallino, Cento, 5 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, when I entrust you to Jesus, where must I place you to give you rest, if not in the loving cavern of the Side of Jesus? In this alone is found that dear balm which inebriates us!

cf. Letter 47, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 November 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

My Jesus, no other motive leads us to lead this life but Your love: to see You one day and to enjoy You face to face, this is our glory, this is the centre of our happiness.

Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear Daughters of Saint Anne, love, love Jesus; make yourselves victims of charity. I envy you!

cf. Letter 14, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 May 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Today my mind is all with you, in our Chapel, before dear Jesus exposed.

cf. Letter 44, to Caterina Rapallino, Genova, 26 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, love Jesus and keep Him always held tight to your heart; from time to time, during the day, bow your head a little towards your heart, and say to Jesus who is hidden within it: “My Love, make me all Yours, and be You all mine, dear Jesus”. Another time you can say to Him: “My Beloved, what are You doing in here, alone, in so small a dwelling? Ah! speak to me, and calm my doubts, confirm me in Your love. Jesus, my Redeemer, give me Your love!”.

Letter 67, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 8 February March 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

If you knew, dear daughter, how much Jesus loves you, you would certainly be mad for Him, and you would do nothing else but hold Him tight to your heart and say to Him: “My Love, speak to me, command me, for I want to do everything that pleases You”.

Letter 82, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, October 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

My daughter, you will feel Jesus within you if you carry out His will, if you listen to His voice; and you will see with what love and with what caresses He will console you; and then you will say: “What my spiritual Mother told me was the truth, and she did everything for my good!” Then you will do without even her caresses, and indeed you will feel a repugnance for them.

* * *

Love, love Jesus, for in Him you will find all that you desire: pleasures, delights, love, caresses, goods, food, drink, rest.

* * *

Today the “novena” of Holy Christmas begins: unite yourself to this wretched Mother of yours, who will keep you held tight to the Child Jesus, so that you may learn to remain always humble, to be always little, so as to grow only in the spirit and in the love of your Bridegroom, and may you be wholly consumed in this.

cf. Letter 91, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 16 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

The day of Holy Christmas draws near, the day of the great ineffable mystery of love, the day on which Jesus, this delightful pledge, comes to us to teach us the way by which we must go, so as to learn to love and to nourish ourselves with this savoury milk. Behold, a God has made Himself little, and is nourished at a mother’s breast, hiding His power for love, reducing Himself to the most humble and poor of babes… Every poor mother always finds somewhere to lay her newborn child; but You, King of heaven and earth, have nothing but a handful of straw and a few linen cloths to wrap You in!… for a fire - in so dreadful a cold season - You were content to stay in the warmth alone of the breath of two beasts of burden, which, recognising You as their Creator, stood turned towards You in a reverent attitude.

cf. Letter 94, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Jesus in the Crib: how many points of meditation for that way of our good which He came to trace out! He left everything: therefore “if you wish to find Me — He says — you must leave everything: every desire, every affection, every self-satisfaction; and you must only drown yourself in Me, who am the sea of every good, and the fountain that will quench your thirst, however burning it may be. You must leave riches, because the riches which I can give you, you will never be able to find on this earth of mud and miseries, however powerful you may be”.

cf. Letter 94, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

I would like to tell you and speak to you of this dear Love… My daughter, love, for charity’s sake; and keep all your love for this Being without reserve: all for Him, yes, all!

cf. Letter 95, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 23 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

In the Heart of dear Jesus, delightful dwelling, I would like to see you melted away!

* * *

Dear Daughter of Saint Anne, if your days are bitter in this valley of miseries, just as sweet and consoling will be the Eternity you are to have, always with Jesus; but if now you flee from Him, how can you hope to enjoy Him? Ah, no: make your Holy Communion: do not leave your Treasure, otherwise you will become poor. When one has Jesus, one has the whole world.

cf. Letter 151, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 October 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

May Jesus be in your heart and on your lips

* * *

May Jesus consume you with the fire of His Divine Love; and in the outpouring of that Blood which He shed from His Side, may He inebriate you.

Letter 255, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 22 November 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

What consolation I feel merely in pronouncing this word: “to give pleasure to God”; and still more, if there is vividly awakened in me the sweet thought of being, or of being able to become, His delight, I feel quite beside myself, so much so that if I had to face the most cruel martyrdom, I should feel nothing. Who can doubt it? Will there perhaps be a soul who thinks differently, and does not feel what I say? I do not believe it! but only if I knew that there was someone who felt it more than I, I should weep, and weep much; and with great effort I would wish to get ahead of her (that is, to surpass her).

Letter 14, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

The Heart of Jesus is so beautiful and so loving that there are no phrases that can express it. In this most vast Heart charity blazes: she is its queen. Therefore, whoever has not charity will not be able to share in this most blazing Love of His.

cf. Letter 14, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I desire one thing of you, and it is that you try to study how to love God with a love wholly pure and ardent and inflamed; if you attain this, I will say to you: “do what you will, for you will do everything well”. Love and do what you will, said Saint Augustine. Yes, my daughter, love this God our Father, and you will do everything with relish.

Letter 41, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 5 April 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My Jesus, what more than this Work ought to be dear to Your Heart?… what ought to be dear to Your Heart, if not that Your Father be glorified? These poor souls, the “Daughters of Saint Anne”, have Him continually on their lips, and in all their actions they invoke Him, they keep Him in their hearts, because they love Him as a Father, placing in Him all their good.

Letter 60, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Roma, 1 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

(June). What a beautiful month, dear daughters! There is no need even to read the point of “meditation”, having the Heart of Jesus open: there, there, my dear ones, bring your mind, your heart: there you will find everything, and you will rest sweetly.

cf. Letter 64, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Roma, 6 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Listen, dear daughter, I have a thorn, and do you know what this thorn is?… it is seeing that you love God little. You will say to me: “how can you know this?” Here it is, my dear daughter: the little patience in adversities, in the small denials of the will, in sufferings, the little resignation to the Divine Will, that irritability as soon as there appears, even only in the distance, the prospect of having to leave the milk of sweetness; and when at once, without heeding the offence to God, one grows upset, gives scandal, speaks loudly in time of strict silence… My God, do not these things speak clearly that this heart is empty of Your love, and that it is still swathed in flesh? Consume it, consume it, and make it all Yours, for ever.

Letter 137, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 20 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My daughter, do you know who sweetens all our sorrow? it is the love of God; this makes us desire suffering, so that in it all the dregs of the creature may be consumed, and all our senses may remain mortified.

Letter 158, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 5 February 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

When one loves, how welcome suffering becomes to us, how sweet the crosses! the weight is felt no longer, but instead everything is changed into sweetness and gentleness, and little by little we become hungry for them. Ah! how sweet it is to love God in suffering.

Letter 158, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 5 February 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

My God, whoever has not tasted the love of God may be called a poor wretch, dead to all that is greatest and most sublime and holy in heaven and on earth.

cf. Letter 158, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 5 February 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Whoever has loved little will taste little of the Beloved, and her portion will be very small.

Letter 158, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 5 February 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Let us try to love much, so as one day to possess the love of that God who so much desires to pour into us this balm of His, which inebriates us all and one day will make us blessed.

Letter 158, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 5 February 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Only from the Heart of Jesus can we draw love: let us do violence to this Heart, and we will have everything.

cf. Letter 158, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 5 February 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Sincerity, charity, the love of God is the only thing we need; all the rest is a mere nothing, and less than nothing.

Letter 225, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 29 April 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

My daughter, for charity’s sake I urge you to make your Holy Communion; your coldness, which wishes to stay far from so immense a treasure, frightens me. Think that this is He who gives everything and from whom we can have everything. He is our life, our peace, our comfort in our adversities. Ah! my Daughter, think that we have everything from this good God.

Letter 265, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 20 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Communion! my dear one, for pity’s sake, do not withdraw from this fountain of graces, because whoever stays far from it can have nothing.

Letter 267, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 24 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The Heart of our God says: “Whoever feeds on Me will be sure of eternal life”; what then?… Ah! if we could feed on it every moment, every second; what happiness would it not be for us to have nothing to feed on but this Most Holy Bread! If we cannot have it bodily, let us try to receive it spiritually; let us make a lively resolution of it in the morning, saying to dear Jesus: “today I want to receive You continually, and I will keep my thought always occupied in making spiritual Communions”. Little by little it comes about (as a consequence) that we make a habit of it, and even while speaking we invoke the sweet name of our Beloved Jesus with an act of love, and we say to Him: “Come, O my Bridegroom, come, this heart wants You; it can no longer stay without You, come!”.

Letter 277, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 26 July 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

You say, dear daughter, that you are cold: we cannot always be fervent, because this is the way our Jesus deals with His brides: today a little sweet, tomorrow dryness and sadness. Saint Teresa used to say that she was very glad in the time of dryness, because she knew that her Jesus was preparing a little sweet for her; on the other hand, in the time of sweetness she trembled, because she knew that the bitterness would come after.

Letter 287, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 26 August 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Ah! what contentment!… to be united to the good God!… but you, my dear one, if you stay far from this dear and most loving One, I fear you will never be able to have anything. Go, go and suck the honey of sweetness: He is its essence; run to His fountain and drink and be inebriated. Oh, blessed moment, when I will see my dear daughter drunk with this wine!

Letter 152, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 14 November 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Dear daughter, your poor Mother keeps you always close, so that you may become a heroine of virtue and of love.

cf. Letter 161, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Piacenza, 9 December 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

I would like you, dear daughter, to come at last to understand that we must have no other “object” to occupy our thought, our heart, but God alone: to live for Him alone, crucified for Him. Dear daughter, what use is the whole entire world if we do not have God? None, less than nothing!

cf. Letter 15, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 10 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

The love of creatures is nothing but a contagion which grows ever greater in them, and gives off ever more the stench of a corpse, because it does nothing but turn us into corpses and make us brutes, idolaters of the flesh and of the senses, a horrible thing, repulsive beyond measure.

Letter 15, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 10 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

The love of a God, all most perfect and most pure, most savoury and most sweet, purifies us the more, beautifies us, makes us fragrant with a most sweet ether, feeds our soul! Reflect, dear daughter: all this lasts for an eternity! Courage, then: a brief suffering for an eternal joy.

cf. Letter 15, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 10 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughter, … the time draws near when Jesus leaves His Mother and goes to begin His “passion”. Let us try, dear daughter, to make some little provision, so as to be able to follow Him and to relieve some torment, in those forty-seven days which He spent in the desert, deprived of everything and exposed to such cruel inclemencies of the weather. Nothing else pleases dear Jesus so much as that little attention in fulfilling our duty exactly.

cf. Letter 16, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 17 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

What does the Sacred Heart say?… Love Me, My bride; all your love to Me; leave the flesh once and for all, come within Me, and you will find such sweetness and relish as will be different from what your poor heart has held until now. I will give you a certain liqueur that will strengthen you, will satisfy you, and you will no longer fear being deprived of it, because I am the most faithful Bridegroom.

Letter 121, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 22-25 October 1871 J — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughter, be of good heart and always held tight to the Heart of Jesus, your dear and beautiful Bridegroom: in Him is found the whole world: relatives, friends, sisters, brothers; and your heart, truly united to His, will remain fully satisfied with every kind of love, because the love of Jesus is the essence of love, and in the essence lies everything.

Letter 18, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 25 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Be cheerful, and keep your mind in God; thus you will find me, and you will not have to feel any pain at being deprived of being near me, because you will be held tight to me in that dear side of Jesus; and how much nearer one is in this than in being near in presence! Yes, my dear daughter, believe it: I hope that, growing in the school of Divine Love, you will learn to reason in this language.

Letter 88, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 19-21 August 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

You tell me, dear daughter, that you fear to detain me by speaking of God, lest you should weary me; ah! dear daughter, if I found souls who would speak to me of Him for a whole night and a day, they would do nothing but stir in me the longing to hear of Him more and more; ah! who will ever succeed in satisfying me? No one; only You, my God, in Your beatitude. Speak to me always of Jesus: you will never go wrong.

Letter 394, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 30 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Try to make your Holy Communion, and while you receive Jesus tell Him to heal you perfectly and to go and put balm upon your ill, and then peace.

Letter 174, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, December 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us leave to God the care of all that concerns us.

Letter 50, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 2 May 1871 L — vol. 2

* * *

Love Jesus, and be content.

* * *

What a beautiful day tomorrow is: the day of the Holy Spirit! Ah! would that God might fill your hearts with this fire, and furnish your minds with heavenly light, so that you may direct your communities well, and instil the true spirit of the Rules, love for Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, and give good example.

cf. Letter 236, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 18 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Hold fast to God, dear daughter, and love Him, and you will see what He will give you!

cf. Letter 347, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 November 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

What a sweet month is that of the Heart of Jesus, which receives our every wretched sigh. So then, my beloved daughter, bring everything into this Heart, and you will find everything; say to Him thus: “Dear Jesus, let me too taste a single little drop of Your most sweet nectar”, and you will see that Jesus will give you everything, because He desires to hear Himself sought, and to give it to whoever truly longs for it with faith and frankness. God gives this to the simple and not to the wise of the world.

Letter 67, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Roma, 7-11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My daughter, learn to love dear God and to give to Him alone all your affections, all to Him, to live for Him, to love Him alone. O love of our Good, when will it be that I will see my dear daughter inflamed with Your love? She is spending her life, ready to give all her blood for You; give her, then, the strength and the love to spend it. Forward, and courage.

Letter 193, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Roma, 13 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

He whom we serve is a good Father, a most faithful Bridegroom, incapable of being unfaithful to us: we must not fear.

cf. Letter 222, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Roma, 15 March 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

My God, give me a hundred arms, that I may spend them all for You!

cf. Letter 329, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Genova, 25 September 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Dear daughter, how happy I should be if you confirmed your love towards me by giving me proofs that you love God greatly! I assure you that this contentment would bring much relief to my oppressions. Come, then, come with me to Calvary for love of our Crucified One, to be for Him alone and together with Him on the Cross.

cf. Letter 340, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 October 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Ah! dear daughters, when you have the love of God, blessed are you! nothing will remain for you to desire: only to increase in it until you are consumed in Him!

* * *

In God I find all that is necessary for me: He fills the emptiness left by creatures; oh, how good He is to me! Yes, I cannot help telling you with all the strength of my soul: Love, love God, and then you will have everything.

Letter 22, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 January 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Oh, yes! my portion is charity.

Letter 322, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Roma, 5 April 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Dear daughter, you speak to me of sacrifices, and I see that they are hard for you to bear! Dear daughter, what is there more beautiful, more dear, for one who loves Him who alone is worthy of our love, in order to possess His love? oh, dear daughter, what does it take?… sacrifices, crosses, pains, suffering!… and to fight like true soldiers of the eternal “homeland”, where who reigns?… who?… the most beautiful and most sweet of all the beings we have in heaven and on earth; His name is Divine Love; and only to those who knew how to fight well and to conquer, and whose breast is covered with medals of honour; yes, only to those is it given to taste the most pure balm of this love. Oh! may it consume you, may it burn you to ashes!

cf. Letter 58, to Sr. A. Agnese Sismondini, Piacenza, 1 May 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

“Love, love, and then do what you will”, says Saint Augustine. Yes; whoever loves cannot displease the beloved, so that in all she does she keeps that sweet fear of erring and displeasing; holy fear, sweet and dear, you are nothing else but a chain that binds me tight to the Heart of Love.

Letter 58, to Sr. A. Agnese Sismondini, Piacenza, 1 May 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

May the Lord engrave His Name in your heart, and so may it remain there for an eternity.

Letter 220, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 29 December 1878 — vol. 5

MY dear Daughters, you have the means to make yourselves saints, and saints soon. Blessed are you, when that day comes on which you can say: “I am dying because I have worn myself out too much in the works of charity!” And then be sure that our dear Mother Saint Anne will be waiting at the gates of Paradise to receive you, and you will be blessed for all eternity.

Letter 11, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 23 April 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Take comfort, you who labour for your Jesus, because in touching the sick with charity (and with that so great charity which our dear Mother Saint Anne had), in touching those infirm souls, you touch Jesus who is found in them. Ah! what a thought, my Daughters!

cf. Letter 11, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 23 April 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

I assure you that I feel myself dying with the desire to come and be with you, to take part (in that hospital) in your works of charity. Yes, soon, I hope; and it is this alone that makes me work night and day, so as to be able to fly to those whom I love so much, namely those sick people and you, my dear daughters. Ask Saint Anne to obtain for you her charity.

cf. Letter 11, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 23 April 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Remember often that you must imitate the charity of your Mother Saint Anne, true charity towards one’s neighbour: to love the one who suffers, to suffer with him.

cf. Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

All the Daughters must keep before them the Divine Model, Jesus, in order to correct their way of thinking and of acting, especially with regard to that charity which I so much recommend, and in which our Mother Saint Anne was so great.

* * *

Ah! dear daughter, I assure you that merely in writing words that speak of charity, I feel a strong desire within me… My God, calm this fire, for it makes me suffer too much! Ah! when will that day come on which I will be able to give vent to such ardour?… But what am I writing? Forgive me, dear daughter; you see, when this thought takes hold of my mind, I cannot contain it.

cf. Letter 20, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1–10 August 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Every action of ours done against our own bad will, but only for His love, will always be pleasing to the Eternal One. Let us see creatures in Him and love them.

Letter 154, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 October 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Pray, and love one another all with the same love, and try to attain that beautiful unity of thinking and of acting, so that all together you may form one heart alone, one thought alone, because you all tend towards one centre, which is God.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

True charity among you must be so sincere that one’s own good must also be the good of one’s sister. If you become thus, the Spirit of God will reign in you.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

How sweet it is to us when we can offer relief to one in need; how we feel awakening in us an affection wholly pure towards those souls, however repugnant; and if our very blood were needed (to help them), we would quickly draw it from our veins to satisfy the poor man or the sick one.

Letter 14, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

When I speak of charity, it seems to me that I should never stop; I find everything in it: every consolation… everything, in a word.

cf. Letter 14, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I wish to hear news of the care of the sick; let us hope that the good Jesus will deign to let Himself be cared for by the poor Daughters of Saint Anne.

Letter 54, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 22 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughter, you did very well to send (for nursing care) to that lady. What does it matter if she has such an illness?… is she not perhaps worthy of being cared for?… indeed, for my part, I bear her a special affection and compassion.

cf. Letter 72, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Roma, 16 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Love one another, and may charity be what accompanies you in all your actions.

Letter 198, to the Sisters of the House in Via della Morte, Genova, 25 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

God be blessed! what consolation I feel when I hear that peace reigns in you and among you. May God preserve it for you; poor creature that I am, every day I pray the good God to give it to you.

Letter 146, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Genova, 7 November 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

God wishes to be served with cheerfulness; and it is always of benefit to our soul, because in this way our neighbours are treated with affability and gentleness; on the contrary, when we let ourselves be taken by bad humour, it comes about that very often acts of discourtesy and of little charity are committed towards our neighbours.

cf. Letter 3, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Città, 1-5 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughter, make yourself all things to all, and above all for the “gems”, the dear sick.

cf. Letter 89, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Piacenza, 9 May — vol. 4

* * *

I hold tight to my Crucified One (the teachers), so that they may give to the children — who are entrusted to them — the milk of Holy Religion, that they may grow up true servants of the Lord and good Catholics.

* * *

Courage, dear daughters, it is time to labour and to carry out great missions to win souls for God! Too many are falling headlong into the abyss of hell. Courage; blood for blood: Jesus on the cross, all torn in His flesh; so must we be!

Letter 274, to Sr. A. Gesuina Moroni, Roma, 4 January 1877 ’ — vol. 4

* * *

When Jesus sends us sick sisters, we must not be afraid or displeased, but we must hold them as so many gems.

cf. Letter 182, to Sr. A. Antonietta Gallinari, Piacenza. 17 August 1880(‘78)’ — vol. 6

* * *

Oh, I would like to see you… in the sweet hospital wards, near the bed of Jesus, now dressing His wounds, now doing for Him what He needs!… and so may He give to your heart those sweet throbs of love; every morning I tell Him to consume you in it. Oh, sweet love, consume my dear daughters, so that I may have them with me in Your kingdom always, for an eternity, for I hope that through the pure mercy of God I may go there.

cf. Letter 207, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 17 December 1878 — vol. 5

LET us not deceive ourselves: in the works of the Lord patience and sacrifice are needed. Sacrifices please God more than great promises and anything else. Jesus sacrificed Himself for us, and until the last evening He drank the bitter chalice.

Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage: suffering is indispensable. Look at Peter: “Come”, the Master said to him; and he, without thinking that he had a family and other things, ran at once. And so have done all those who have followed the Saviour. Certainly this Master had no other recreation than to go alone in search of the lost sheep, heeding neither food nor clothing; and together with Him the Apostles went to suffer hunger and thirst; and, to say everything in one word, “to suffer” was their refreshment.

cf. Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

“Whoever will follow me,” says the Master, “let him take up his cross and follow me.” What language, then, is this? O blessed souls, the Heavenly Bridegroom gives us that treasure which the world does not know: the Cross. And to His beloved Brides He holds it out, and indeed He seeks that it be heavy, and He lets them taste His delights, so that they may find that Cross small, even those Brides who drag it along.

cf. Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Since the treasure of the Cross is also burdensome at the beginning, it is enough never to stop, even at the cost of having to drag it, for it is then that Jesus is moved to compassion and helps us to carry it.

cf. Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

When we fall, we must take heart. Let us humble ourselves before our Bridegroom for our misery, but let us call Him to our aid, as Father of pity and of love, and with words full of compunction let us beg Him, as little children do, to be pleased to lift us up and adorn us, so as to be less deformed in His eyes. Oh, how this Love delights to see Himself treated so! not as certain Souls do, who believe Him a tyrant. If He permits us to fall, it is to humble us all the more and make us pleasing in the eyes of His Father.

cf. Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

I hear that you are still so tormented by sadness; but — my dear daughter — do you hope to have consolation and peace as long as we dwell in this tearful valley of weeping? You know what is found in suffering, do you not? Jesus is found there, the dear One of our heart, the very being of our every thought. Well then, all that we do, all of it is for Jesus, dear daughter. Live in tranquillity, therefore: He accepts your sufferings; and in time you will feel the effects of this suffering of yours.

cf. Letter 15, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 13 June 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

For Jesus we must bear everything cheerfully, even depriving ourselves of what is dearest to us; so our dear Mother Saint Anne teaches us.

* * *

I am suffering beyond measure, but most content to suffer as it pleases Jesus; and I hope it will be in discount of my sins.

* * *

Dear one of Jesus, be of good heart, for your Mother Saint Anne loves you, and takes account of all the sufferings, of all the desolations of her Daughter; and she keeps refreshments ready for her which — in due time — she will send her. Now, my dear, is the time to suffer, if one day we wish to have a fair rejoicing.

Letter 37, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 3 October 1867 — vol. 1

Our Father Saint Francis of Assisi used to say: “So great is the good I await that every pain is a delight to me.” I assure you, daughter, that if your suffering could be passed on, I would take it all, all upon myself, so as to give back to you that happiness which you desire.

Letter 37, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 3 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Blessed be, and for ever, the will of the good Jesus, who procures for us such dear suffering.

Letter 42, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 20 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, I am in the most dreadful straits. Pray and have others pray, that I may keep peace and cheerfulness alive under the weight of so heavy a cross. I assure you that I am content and that it always seems little to me; but I also know that if He who gives me this relish in suffering were to withdraw ever so little, ah! I would certainly be the ugliest monster, and all would be lost. Ah, good Jesus! He, my Daughter, makes a balsamic ether come forth from the thorns to inebriate us, and I am sure that all of you too will ask Him for it, and He, our Beloved, will give it to you.

cf. Letter 13, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 2 May 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

My system is not to rejoice too much in contentments, and instead to find true joy in the adversities and crosses that Jesus sends us and, as Master, teaches us to embrace.

* * *

If we wish to learn, we must always keep before our eyes the figure of the Redeemer, and gaze upon it continually, and then we will do everything with perfection.

* * *

I implore for all of you the Holy Blessing from Heaven, that it may strengthen you in suffering.

cf. Letter 29, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 19 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage, my daughter, it is the time to suffer: but Jesus will make you happy!

* * *

Now that we are on the mount, we must not lose heart at the crucifixion; rather, we ourselves must prepare the nails for the executioners, for those who bring us so many tribulations, and desire that they be soon driven into us.

cf. Letter 80, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 26 October 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage, my dear, for soon the good Jesus will console you: He has already begun; but let us not grow used to sweets, no! Let us always keep in mind that on Calvary He was not given “vin santo”, but gall and vinegar, and if we are to follow Him, we must desire nothing else but to suffer, to suffer. Long live suffering, yes, long live suffering! I embrace you upon the Cross, my Daughter!

* * *

There is no softer bed than the Cross: this dear pledge contains every delight.

* * *

The purple robe (for Heaven) we cannot have unless we climb upon the Cross: God Himself has left it upon this Holy Wood, the nuptial bed, the bed of His most beloved Brides.

Letter 95, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 23 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage, Daughter; Saint Anne our Mother will reward you, be sure of it, for this is certain for whoever suffers: one day you will see that your pains will be changed into so many gems, your sufferings into jubilation and consolation.

cf. Letter 114, to Carolina Pezzoni, Piacenza, 6 April 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

My God, do, do with this donkey of Yours whatever You will!… When that blessed hand of the Eternal Father strikes us, ah! how sweet are His blows! Yes, my dear, I would do nothing but kiss it and clasp it!

Letter 120, to Carolina Pezzoni, Piacenza, 14 April 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

My daughter, let us profit by these precious moments (of suffering) to store up some little savings for eternal life. One day we will know the value (of suffering), and then we will weep over our neglect of it.

* * *

Courage on the way of Calvary, if you wish to come to be crucified with your Beloved, and to die with Him on the delightful bed of the Cross.

cf. Letter 126, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 27 May 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

To carry the Cross takes strength, courage and generosity.

cf. Letter 131, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 26 June 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Suffer a little longer for the Lord, for He repays everything a hundredfold for one.

* * *

I am truly furnished with lances on every side, but I stay always upon the Cross, crying out: Long live Jesus, may His will be done in us. Patience always in the midst of so many pains… God has so permitted it for our good.

cf. Letter 133, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 2 July 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Suffering may be called a true grace, because it changes this valley of tears for us into a purifying exile.

* * *

To be able to do something pleasing to God is enough to make me find in suffering every kind of happiness.

* * *

New year, new cross: let us prepare to receive it with open arms, for so we will carry it better, and be able to clasp it to our breast, and die upon it.

cf. Letter 175, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Not all days are alike; one must have patience: now by gentle means, now by firm ones, little by little one comes to the end of the work. By the exercise of patience everything is obtained.

Letter 177, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 8 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us take everything from the hands of the Lord, and thank Him for the mercy He shows us.

Letter 177, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 8 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, where are your so cruel pains? I do not find them, because while I look at my Jesus, and then at His Bride (a Daughter of Saint Anne), I see nothing that could be laid upon the smallest of His wounds. I look for her suffering and find none, not even enough to relieve the least sorrow of Jesus.

Letter 180, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 16 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Do your teeth hurt? well then, Jesus had all of His shattered, and His mouth was streaming with blood. Do you find no one to tell your pains and afflictions to?… I see a Father (spiritual) who listens to you and lifts you up, and this poor Mother of yours who would give everything to make you a true “Crucified One”, so as one day to die on the bed of Jesus; and then… then in Paradise for an eternity: there, there is no more cross, there are no more sufferings; only love, love; and it is furnished with all the sweets imaginable.

Letter 180, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 16 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Be cheerful, Daughter, be cheerful, for Jesus is pleased with those who suffer: whoever does not wish to suffer does not wish to love.

cf. Letter 180, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 16 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Respect your habit, for you have one foot in Paradise and the other in the world to carry the Cross.

cf. Letter 185, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and Sr. A. Vincenza, Piacenza, 28 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Jesus wants us upon the Cross: tell me, Daughter, is it not dear to you to die on the “bed” of your Bridegroom? Yes, yes, tell me again that you will die with me so as to live an eternity.

Letter 189, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 6 February 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage, Daughters, a brief suffering for an eternal rejoicing! One day we will be up there among the blessed, if, by the mercy of God, this creature goes there. Then our suffering will seem little to us, and we will be discontented at not having known how to bear more for the love of our God.

cf. Letter 237, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 6 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Today I received your letter full of anguish; what must I answer you?… only that for whoever wishes to follow Jesus this is the road: to suffer and to be in pain; these are the torments of our Master. The pains, the atrocious agony, one may say He began them on the first day of His life.

cf. Letter 239, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Come now, courage, Daughter, courage, soon you will see that the Lord will console you; but with an ounce of patience and two of faith in God you will have everything, I assure you; but peace, little over-subtle reasoning, and day by day embrace the Cross that the Lord sends us. Remember: new days, new crosses.

Letter 239, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

I am most happy when I can say to the Lord: “I offer You a tiny bit of suffering, in return for that most atrocious suffering which You endured from those cruel thorns that were the work of my sins.”

Letter 242, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 17 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Try to take everything from the hands of God. He is for us our every happiness, our every all; and with this conviction everything turns out well for us, and we receive adversities with peace and resignation, turning our thought to the Passion of Jesus; and we remain almost ashamed at seeing a God who for us has suffered so many insults, outrages and every kind of calumny; thus nothing should come to us as new.

Is it any wonder if Jesus gives us a share in His suffering? If we wish to be His, we must eat of the same bread: hardships, pains and sweat, there is its seasoning!… All these things have an end, and they leave us an eternal pledge.

cf. Letter 249, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Sampierdarena, 27 September 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

It is a time of labour and of much suffering in this Work of the Lord. The Church is afflicted, and so everything that belongs to Her suffers anguish and pain from it.

Letter 271, to a Teaching Sister, Città, 28 December 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Sorrows are changed into joy when one suffers for our Lord.

cf. Letter 36, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 23 March 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Oh! what a consoling thing it is when we can open our breast to our dear God, our Sovereign and All, and say to Him: “Deign to look upon our wounds, and all of them, one by one, to number them; and that one which still sheds blood, and, being so open and torn, points to extreme sorrow.” Upon this His gaze rests. What does it do, my blessed Daughter, this most holy gaze?… it dresses it with a balsamic ointment, and it remains numbed, and it pours over the others its most sweet and most savoury nectar, which sweetens everything, and from bitter and painful sores they become most sweet comforts, gentle companions, loving sisters. Alas! my dear, when I recall the most sweet nectar they yield, I would do nothing but speak of it for a hundred years, and I would never grow weary, nor could I be satisfied.

cf. Letter 41, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 5 April 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My God, accept pains, hardships, torments; and may they all be to the advantage of Your Work, and in discount of my purgatory.

* * *

What should I say to the Daughters of Saint Anne?… Only that in the time of trial great strides are made on the way of holiness, and our soul is adorned with virtue, becomes great, and finally — when peace returns — enjoys the fruit (of the trial), sharing in the delights of her beloved Jesus.

Letter 69, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Rome, 11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Patience and suffering are those two great points on which our holiness and eternal happiness rest: a brief suffering for a great rejoicing.

Letter 93, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 1 September 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

God wants us upon the Cross; well then, let us lie well settled upon it, for so, in dying, we will have near us our dear Jesus, our only Love, the Being of our life.

Letter 102, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 20 September 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I share in your troubles, Daughter, and I feel compassion for them, but what is to be done? one thing only: to have recourse to our “all”, Jesus, and to take comfort with Him, telling Him our afflictions, and seeking with them to dress some small wound of His made by our sins. This, I assure you, is enough to relieve our every suffering.

cf. Letter 111, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 15 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

A “Your will be done” said with resignation in time of battles and afflictions is worth more than having the gift of raising the dead to life.

Letter 119, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Illnesses, the Sisters who have died, are true tribulations, and they are sorrows that touch the heart, and one cannot help feeling great pain. But Jesus too wept for Lazarus; Mary wept for her Son and could not be consoled while she held Him lifeless in her arms; supreme for her was the sorrow at seeing Him so ill-treated, so torn in His humanity: at the thought of the pains suffered by Jesus, Mary was drowned in tears and sorrow; and so we, miserable creatures, cannot help feeling a most painful heartbreak, even while we remain resigned to the will of the Eternal Father. Everything must be taken in peace for love of Him.

cf. Letter 119, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughter, you will say: “This blessed Mother can speak of nothing but suffering; always the same story!” My dear, where am I to find a pastime, if I do not stop where I know I have sweetness, love, peace?

cf. Letter 119, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Before entering the Side of Jesus, this “volcano” of love, we must have been cleansed by the scourge and by the foaming soap of suffering.

cf. Letter 119, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Jesus says: plain sweets are made for little girls… if I press my scourge upon the shoulders of one who is weak, I do it out of pure mercy, so as one day to see them beautiful, great and strong in Paradise.

Letter 119, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Today, Friday, I have brought my Daughter into the Side of Jesus, that He may consume her!

cf. Letter 118, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Listen: flee often into this loving cavern of our Jesus, and enter it especially when you are sad and have some affliction; then is the precious moment, for we are sure to find every kind of consolation there; there everything is forgotten, one only tastes…; and no other hunger is felt but that for suffering, because the more laden with pains we are, the more Jesus opens to us His most loving Side, and in those so delightful hiding places we rejoice in a beatitude of anticipated paradise. Only one difference lies between the “paradise” we enjoy here below and that which will be enjoyed in Heaven, and it is this: this one on earth we cannot enjoy, and at present — while we enjoy it — we must hold to our lips the chalice of bitterness; and it is this that pours into our soul the most pure essence of the love of God. This is our Paradise, these are our immense consolations here below, and they are what assure us of an eternal happiness.

cf. Letter 118, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Let us take up our Cross and say to the Eternal Father: “My dear Father, deign to look upon me, and may this gaze of Yours strengthen me, so that I may not only carry this dear Cross upon my shoulders, but courageously hold it clasped to my breast, and that it may then serve me to rest upon it in the last hours of my mortal sleep, so as to be able, at that moment, to say to You:”My Good, I am upon Your bed (the Cross), my Bridegroom, so as soon to rise and come with You to rejoice in Your dwelling.” Suffering, you are that pledge which can bind me with an indissoluble bond to my God.

Letter 118, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 20 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My dear Daughter, do not be troubled by anything; have confidence in God: everything, in the light of this All, is a nothing!

Letter 136, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 18 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

God seems to wish to grant me the grace that my hands become powerless, so much that I can no longer write. How good is our Eternal Father, who satisfies our desires, and in particular with this ugly slave of His, who is truly like a putrid corpse!…

Letter 137, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 20 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughter, the wounds, the sores of Jesus Crucified are our only comfort; they are the balm that heals our sores, and in particular the bitter wounds that certain blades make in our poor breast; and who, if not You, my God, can dress them? The gentle touch of Your hand heals every sorrow: how dear is this Eternal Father of ours, daughter! And Jesus acts as nurse so willingly; and He is skilful, He knows well how, and at the right time, to apply His sweet ointment.

cf. Letter 148, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 27 December 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

These are times of tribulations and crosses: let us try to embrace everything with holy resignation, and let us hold fast to the unshakeable tree of the Cross, so as one day to find ourselves saved and blessed for an eternity.

Letter 252, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Ferrara, 8 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Let courage and resignation be our two shields, to sustain us in all the immense adversities that are found in the Work of the Lord.

cf. Letter 252, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Ferrara, 8 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Blessed are the afflicted, they will be the possessors (of heaven). Therefore all the pains, all the torments make the way for us to arrive there happily. A brief suffering for an eternal rejoicing: what happiness, my beloved Daughters!

Letter 291, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 3 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

For the love of God everything is little!

* * *

You must be strong, Daughter. I feel your pains, and they all descend into my soul; I would like to be able to relieve them by taking everything upon myself, but, dear Daughter, know that after suffering and pain you will have to console yourself with the very pains you now suffer: the good Jesus will come to console you.

Letter 304, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Nizza, 29 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Men have nothing for us but crosses and pains.

Letter 304, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Nizza, 29 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The bed of sickness must serve as a purging of our many faults, so that we may be exempt from Purgatory; instead (if we are not resigned) we heap fault upon fault, and end by having to undergo a Purgatory of many years, and a painful one.

cf. Letter 309, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Nizza, 5 October 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

We must have patience: Saint Anne will see to it; if she sends us sick sisters, she will send us the means to care for them; let us trust in the good God, for we will have everything.

cf. Letter 83, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 14 (March ) April 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Daughter, be at peace, for peace of soul, joined to tranquillity of body, and resigning oneself perfectly in everything to the will of God, does much good to our poor humanity. What happens to the angry? they spoil their liver, and soon become unfit for any service. Courage and peace: may they be your faithful guardians.

cf. Letter 83, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 14 (March ) April 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

It is a time of trial (while we are on earth) and patience is needed. Jesus suffered tribulations of every kind; so it is fitting that we too, who by His mercy are enlisted under His banner, must suffer persecutions. On the day of judgement we will see the rich Dives groaning, and poor Lazarus, full of glory, triumphing in the kingdom of Heaven.

Letter 100, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 30 May 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Suffering must be embraced with pleasure, and never allowed to go to waste.

cf. Letter 138, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Piacenza, 25 October 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Suffering is the true road for going to Paradise and near to our God; for Jesus everything is little; come now, courage; let us not be cast down: we are on the cross, and the embraced cross we have as our inheritance. We do what we can on our part, and the rest we must place in God, because He can do all, and we nothing.

Letter 143, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 29 October 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

May the will of God be fulfilled in us: that is all I desire to have.

Letter 104, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 4 June 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

With patience everything is obtained.

Letter 395, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 31 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

God wills that we suffer; let us kiss His hand in the hour when it strikes us;… it gives me strength to see that our Beloved, our all — God — protects us, and gives help in the midst of so many adversities.

cf. Letter 240, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

I rejoice to feel the weight of my gracious Cross; I take great, great delight in feeling that this wretched humanity bends and writhes; yet it too, bent to the pleasure of the spirit, rejoices in its suffering.

Letter 207, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Sampierdarena, 23–25 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, try once and for all to tame the feeling of that ugly animal, self-love, and then you will see how easy it will be for you to carry the Cross, and it will always seem small to you, just as this poor mother of yours is never sated with the weight of this treasure.

Letter 207, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Sampierdarena, 23–25 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

I am of the opinion (that at times) we must let things pass, and offer everything to Jesus in silence, since these are the precious gems that one day may crown our heads.

cf. Letter 205, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

My Cross is so very large, and I do not know how to take hold of it to embrace it well and clasp it to my breast; and one day — when it pleases my God — to end upon it the last breath of this sorrowful life, and that my bones, laid upon this dear bed, may remain to rest in peace for an eternity. When I take to reasoning thus, a joy floods my whole soul.

Letter 209, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 27 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us take everything with patience and resignation to the will of God; then everything turns out well for us, and so a tribulation, enormous as it is, becomes mild and light.

cf. Letter 231, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 June 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Jesus is pleased with the courageous. He delights to lay a portion of the passion upon their shoulders. Take heart, then, on the way of the Lord, and in everything let us trust in Him; this is the only way to run safely along the road that leads straight to heaven.

cf. Letter 231, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 June 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

The Lord wills to be glorified in adversities.

Letter 12, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 26 April 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, God wants you on a road along which He is wont to lead His beloved ones: it is dark, full of thorns and pains; but do you know what He does when they come to the end of it? He inebriates them with His delightful wine, love, so much that they forget themselves and run thirsting towards suffering; on this road they feel the thorns, but the pricks are sweet to them; they feel the torments of their breast, and these are changed for them into loving heartbeats, for they no longer feel anything, they no longer hear anything but a fiery blaze of love that draws them to seek the Beloved; and if, to reach Him, it were necessary to descend into the abyss of hell, they would descend into those atrocious pains, so as at last to have found their good; not even there would they feel anguish, because this Being sweetens everything, and He is that nectar which lies within the sharpest thorns.

Letter 29, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Sampierdarena, 6 March 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

When God sends us bread (of suffering), we must know how to eat it so as to become strong.

cf. Letter 145, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 12 December 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

My Daughter, I exhort you never to grow weary of suffering, and with peace and resignation bear that illness which the good Jesus sends you. Put out of your head the thought — “Must I always be an invalid?” — and saying to God: “Rather die soon than remain like this.” An ugly word, which is on the lips of worldly people, who — the unfortunate ones — find no other good and happiness than in enjoying perishable things, placing everything in them, as though this unhappy earth produced fruits of consolation and of life; far otherwise: it is nothing but the sharpest thorns and eternal death! That is the produce it yields, and unfortunate are those who find themselves furnished with this alone on the day of the great passing; blessed — on the contrary — are those who have lived for heaven, and for whom this earthly exile has served to gain an eternal dwelling.

* * *

To suffer, only to suffer is our inheritance in this tearful valley.

cf. Letter 27, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

I pray Jesus to give everything (the suffering) to me and to unburden all of you, for I assure you that it is very dear to me and I have no other treasure on this earth but suffering: yes, you are my treasure!

Letter 27, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughters, God bless you all; drink deeply from the cup of suffering.

cf. Letter 27, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

The tribulations are without number; they bow my back, but we must take courage and try to die upon the Cross, victorious with Jesus. Oh! blessed moment when we will breathe our last on the bed of the Cross.

Letter 155, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 20 November 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Blessed patience! If so it pleases the Lord, let us too take delight in His pleasure, so as to make every drink sweet for ourselves, even though it be made of gall.

Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and the Sisters of the Community, Genova, 25 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

God alone is for us; men… I cannot understand how man seeks the destruction of good, and how very little is the good that reigns in the world! Alas, the hand of God can no longer hold back from coming to strike us: everything goes according to the perverse world; what horror!

Letter 180, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 19 January 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Let us lay everything in the Heart of God the Father: so our thoughts will grow calm.

Letter 182, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 22 January 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Pray that — if it pleases God — I may be able to work; let Him not take suffering away from me; but (let Him give me such strength) that I may be able to work.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 18 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

May the will of God be what consumes and destroys us.

cf. Letter 315, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Nizza, 9 September 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Everything that God sends us is always for our good, and so that we may gain ever more merit.

Letter 341, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Piacenza, 23 October 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

The flesh groans under the weight of a prolonged martyrdom in this valley of sorrow and anguish; where does it find its refreshment?… in that infinite Being in whom everything is found, because if the flesh suffers, the spirit rejoices, and so sorrow becomes sweet.

Letter 22, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 January 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Patience and courage always;… everything comes to an end; away, away with melancholy, which is the devil’s net. Courage…

cf. Letter 89, to Sr. A. Gesuina Moroni, Piacenza, 28 June 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

I always offer the Lord your hearts, Daughters, your will, that God the Father may do with them what He thinks best, and give you strength, courage and living faith to do everything for Him alone and nothing, nothing for the earth; for oh, how sweet it is to suffer for Jesus!… how many times I have longed to be among you (to work and to suffer), but I am not worthy of it: my infamies hold back my steps and prevent me from running swiftly;… and I am always at the foot of Golgotha, awaiting the day of my departure to climb Calvary: it is there alone that the beloved is found, and I, dear Daughters, am barely at the bottom of this mount, eager to climb… oh, blessed are you if you arrive there; tell my Jesus that I am dying of desire for Him. Oh, you will find Him, you will kiss Him, and I… pray and say every day: “Hear her and give her what she asks of You.”

cf. Letter 207, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 17 December 1878 — vol. 5

COURAGE and peace: when you are in anguish, call upon Jesus, and you will see that He will console you. Go to the foot of the Altar and say thus: “I intend to unite myself in prayer together with my Mother Rosa,” and ask for what you desire: if you are ill in body, ask Him for bodily health; if in spirit, tell Him that you wish to love Him, and with humility pray Him to come into your heart to bring you peace, union with Him, love of neighbour, charity, obedience to Superiors. Tell Him that you wish to be His faithful and loving Bride, and that you desire to become a perfect religious.

cf. Letter 8, to Giovanna Bixio, Cento, 20 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Have recourse to God often during the day, for so you will find yourselves more tranquil in your Communion.

cf. Letter 16, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 June 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Pray, dear daughters, for prayer is the only weapon with which to defend oneself from so many insidious dangers.

Letter 17, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

As for the great dryness you suffer, I assure you that if you are resigned, your Mother Saint Anne will console you when you least expect it.

cf. Letter 37, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 3 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *
