Courage, my dear ones, pray much; laugh little; pray much and meditate a great deal, for you always have the means to meditate, seeing Jesus in the sick, and so the meditation on the Passion of Jesus will come easily to you.

Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

I hope that I will leave you well settled before I die.

Letter 26, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 4 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear Daughter, yes, “Daughter”, even though the world wishes to tear this name from you; but God will confirm it to you.

Letter 44, to Caterina Rapallino, Genova, 26 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

I, miserable as I am, will offer your prayers with mine, so that Jesus may be consoled in the midst of your crosses.

* * *

Courage always, my Daughter, for everything will be set right, and the ugly infernal monster will never, never win, and his efforts will be useless! Let us always hope in the mercy of the Lord.

* * *

God bless you; and if my prayers, Daughter, are acceptable to Him, believe indeed that in Paradise you will have a place near the Holy Mother. And if it pleases His Divine Majesty to forgive this mother of yours her sins and give her Paradise, we will be near each other.

Letter 135, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 3 July 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughters of Saint Anne, my beloved ones, courage, for one day you will see your God, and you will enjoy the fruit of your labours; and whoever has procured more of them for herself, the greater will be her beatitude.

Letter 145, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 16 September 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Prayer is the key of graces: it opens the treasury of the Lord.

Letter 147, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 September 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughters, pray, for it is the time to pray and to act, labouring tirelessly for Jesus.

cf. Letter 179, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 10 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

The heart of this poor Mother of yours is torn when she sees laughing in church; or on certain evenings, when the Rosary and the prayers are said half asleep. Alas, alas, how will they ever reach the so delicate ear of our Eternal Father?… Ah, instead they will be so many wounds to the Heart of Jesus, our all.

Letter 217, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 May 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us pray; yes, offer fervent prayers to the Heart of Jesus, that He may move the hearts of good people to help the Work of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. He alone can… and in this Work He must exert Himself, since it belongs to His Eternal Father.

Letter 60, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 1 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

The whole world, together with its joys, is a nothing in comparison with an immensity of heavenly goods.

Letter 153, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Nizza, 18 January 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughter, if you are sorrowful, run to the church and pour out your heart to Jesus, weep (with Him), and then, once you have dried your tears, back to work again, all to all, and full of sweet emotion, so as to pass it on to others.

cf. Letter 233, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

I pray every day, every moment.

* * *

We must try to be together for an eternity, because here (on this earth) everything is a nothing and passes so quickly that one does not even notice it; but an eternity is long!

cf. Letter 263, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 14 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Strong courage, for one day, if we have fought well, we will wear the great decoration of love upon our breast, and together we will be for an eternity: a great word is this, which weighs as much as a whole world!

Letter 277, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 26 July 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

He who guides and governs the “Daughters of Saint Anne”, Mother of the Immaculate, is above all: He will set everything right.

cf. Letter 291, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 3 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

I pray for all those who are the cause of troubles and pains, and so — I am sure — will all of you do; and in this way we are sure to tread that safe path which leads us to the kingdom of Heaven.

Letter 291, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 3 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Pray, and you will see that you will obtain everything.

Letter 292, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 4 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

One day we will be together for an eternity of rejoicing; there (in Heaven) the torments will have passed, our pains will have ceased, we will have only rejoicing as our inheritance; and, always united, we will taste the fruit of the sweat poured out in our labours.

cf. Letter 144, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Piacenza, 29 October 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Courage and onward, Daughters, for one day we will be at rest for an eternity.

Letter 163, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 15 December 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Without prayer we are fruitless trees, and we can give nothing good, and our fruits (if we bear any) will always be unripe.

Letter 131, to Maddalena Carmeli, end of September 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

For the Sacred Heart I desire the adoration of the little girls; I desire it to be exact: I count on these prayers, which will open the “sack of Providence”.

* * *

Let us hope that the dear Sacred Heart of Jesus will pour out His graces upon us, and so His “providence” in all things.

cf. Letter 80, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Rome, 1-3 July 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughters, I commend to you meditation and the works of piety, for these are what keep us firm and well settled in our dear vocation; without this (prayer) everything is lost: whoever does not pray is damned, that is most certain.

Letter 191, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 7 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

I trust in your prayers to obtain all that I desire for the Work.

cf. Letter 244, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Rome, 15 April 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

My dear Daughter, courage, for great is the crown that the good God has prepared for you, if you persevere.

cf. Letter 245, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 15 April 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Ah! my dear Daughter, one day indeed we will no longer have either to write or to feel the anxiety of receiving news of one another, but we will be held close together with our Good, to enjoy Him for an eternity. Then all our pains will seem few to us, seeing that they are what brought us a great good. Courage; long live the Cross with suffering, long may it live!

Letter 249, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 20 April 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Prayers are the adornment of our actions. If we render to our God an imperfect work, He will certainly set it aside and not even look at it; but if it is adorned and embellished by prayers, then indeed it will draw His gaze, and He will take delight in us. Ah, what beatitude without equal!… we, the delight of God!… what joy; there is nothing on this earth that resembles it.

cf. Letter 340, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 October 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

My Daughters will be observant in prayers and at meditation. Saint Teresa said that whoever does not meditate is not sure of being saved. Yes, in meditation we learn to love, and whoever comes to meditate well is sure to obtain the love of God.

cf. Letter 348, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 3 November 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

When I am upset and do not find much recollection, I pass at once to meditating on Judas betraying his Master, and then I feel so united with my God in sorrow that I cannot help weeping.

* * *

Let us take comfort, for our place in Heaven is there, no one can take it from us: once we arrive there, we will rest for an eternity.

* * *

Let us bless the Lord for having given us the grace to be able to rest our hopes in Him alone.

Letter 395, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 31 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

I have no other treasure than prayer; from it I have everything, and with it I obtain all courage and the hope that one day we will find our labours at the Throne of God the Judge, and that they will defend us from falling headlong into the abyss, as we deserve.

* * *

I hope in the mercy of the Lord that you will be rewarded by Him; and so also by this poor mother of yours. Courage, for the time of tribulations is short, but soon spring comes: “Jesus”, most loving flower, who will comfort you.

cf. Letter 212, to Sr. A. Guglielma Merli, Piacenza, 20 December 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Daughters, courage, for the way is very painful, but just as beautiful is the dwelling we will go to inhabit.

Letter 275, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 4 April 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

See to it that you do not omit your prayers, your meditation; adjust the timetable, do them either before or after, but omit nothing.

* * *

Oh! blessed are you, who for Jesus have crossed the sea: you are running a fine road on which to become saints, all the more because you are ready to undergo martyrdom.

cf. Letter 311, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 9 June 1879 — vol. 5

KEEP yourselves humble, for this is the only road by which not to fall and to become saints.

cf. Letter 16, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 June 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Ah! we can never be furnished enough with humility; and blessed are we if we could be trampled upon by all! We are never so loved by our Jesus as when, to worldly eyes, we appear useless and lowly creatures.

* * *

My daughters, seek to be the servants of all.

cf. Letter 35, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 26 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Ah! my sisters and daughters, for charity’s sake, keep yourselves low, if you wish one day to be great in Paradise, the only aim of our many labours.

Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

I am overwhelmed with work, and always in poor health. Dear Daughter, this donkey bends under the heavy weight that the Lord is pleased to lay upon its back! The will of the Lord be done.

cf. Letter 64, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 19 January 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

What consolation for me when you hold yourselves annihilated in everything, and seek to please only your Bridegroom Jesus.

* * *

Humility, you are the queen of every virtue! Dear Eternal Father, will You give this miserable creature, before she dies, the consolation of seeing in the House of the glorious Saint Anne this beautiful gem shining in all Your daughters and mine? Then indeed my head will rest joyfully on the pillow of death and, smiling at so great a consolation, will remain with You for an eternity.

Letter 94, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

(A God in our heart!) The very thought exalts us and, at the same time, annihilates us: God in the creature and the creature one with the Creator!… and to arrive at this, you see, dear Jesus is a Child; therefore He wants us to become little children, and to grow only with Him; and He wants to grow in us, giving us His Food and strengthening us with the precious Wine that He changes into His Blood. So He wants us to live in this life, so as then to come into His presence with the purple robe, enamelled with His Blood.

cf. Letter 95, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 23 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

God makes skeletons live again; and if it so pleases Him, He will keep this donkey on its feet as long as the poor Daughters of Saint Anne have need of it.

* * *

Let us remember, my dear Daughters, that we have the model of holy humility: Jesus. And the Church keeps us occupied in these days (of Lent) teaching us how to imitate this model of every virtue. Beginning with His going to the Jordan: what abasement! the most perfect, the most pure God-Man willed to submit to being — like the sinner — purified with the water of Holy Baptism in the Jordan; but Heaven opened, and a voice that could not contain itself said: “This is my Son…”. Jesus, what are You doing?… enough; but no: to greater torments He goes to submit His delicate humanity!…

Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us place ourselves in the presence of God, and receive everything from His hands. Just as we are always convinced that in all we do in this Work we are directed by Him, so, should we find in ourselves any good accomplished, it is wrought by the hand of our Creator; and if in anything we see ourselves at fault, and if what we have done has turned out badly, it is nothing but our own work, by which good Jesus wished to make us touch with our hands that every time we turn away from Him, we are a mere nothing, and less than nothing.

Letter 203, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 13 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us hope in the Lord: to Him be everything; to us the confusion, the humiliation, the annihilation, the shame. Truly I am nothing but a wretched servant of the Lord.

cf. Letter 37, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 25 March 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Jesus is all patience and meekness; He is also charity and love. With these virtues our Holy Mother Saint Anne was likewise adorned.

* * *

The blows which this poor “Work” (the Institute) receives are the fruit of my iniquities. If it so pleases God, let us adore the divine Majesty.

* * *

Dear Jesus, I am so foul with the stench of my iniquities, and yet, my Good, You still deign to stay with me and to come into me!

Letter 137, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 20 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughter, for charity’s sake let us stay humble, otherwise Jesus will humble us. Yes, this I assure you: one act of vainglory, and at once God with His dear hand humbles us down to the abyss of our nothingness; one act of humility, and behold, the dear Eternal Father comforts us by making His work shine forth.

Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear Daughter, I recommend to you the practice of the virtue of humility, and I beseech you for the love of God, and for the love you say you bear me, because without it (this virtue) I will not be able to see you run along the way of perfection.

Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Without humility one cannot enter Paradise.

Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

From now on it will be your concern to come to have humility deeply rooted in your heart.

* * *

Honours are the plague of the soul.

cf. Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Superior, treat your Daughters with a Mother’s love, without embittering them; deal with them calmly and bear with them. Remember that they are poor creatures who labour for Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate.

cf. Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I recommend meekness to you, dear daughter, because this is the true character of a “Daughter of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate”. If we are to imitate the Holy Mother, this is how we must be (meek); otherwise we will never be recognised as daughters of so holy a Mother, and we will remain among the number of the reprobate.

Letter 233, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Keep yourself humble, dear daughter, if you want God to assist you.

cf. Letter 249, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 5 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

It is a very beautiful thing to know that we are nothing, and that the work is for God and of God, the most mighty Sovereign, Ruler of heaven and earth. He casts down and raises up in an instant all of us, (who are) misery and confusion.

Letter 252, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Ferrara, 8 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Man is nothing; and the creature who trusts in her own strength always comes out of it put to shame and confounded, and having lost the peace of her heart.

cf. Letter 265, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 20 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Listen, you ask me, dear daughter, whether you may ask the S. M. for your embroidery and other things. Yes, my dear, do so, but gently; and although you know that these things are yours and belong to you by right, I wish you to ask for them as a charity. Yes, my most beloved Daughter, this is what pleases the Lord: humility pleases Him so much. Ah! my treasure, when will I possess you? Humility, humility! treasure of all treasures!

cf. Letter 147, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Genova, 8 November 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

The Lord humbles us to atone for our frailties.

Letter 151, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 13 November 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

We are poor servants of the Lord, and our work must be a source of satisfaction to our good God, our Father.

cf. Letter 395, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 31 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

If I could be a “thousand” to labour in the work of the Lord, I would do it; I only regret that I am nothing but a wretched walking bier.

Letter 206, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 22 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, correct with calm and patience.

Letter 9, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Città, January 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Do go to Communion, but for eight days, at recreation time, you are to ask your Daughters (the sisters) to forgive the scandal you have given them, so as to satisfy Divine Justice, and with this penance to cancel the fault.

Letter 3, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Città, 1-5 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Away with irritability, away with sulking; be always cheerful, in adversity as in fair weather and in times of enjoyment; always the same in the presence of God the Father, always joyful. I too, in the midst of so many pangs, make everyone laugh and laugh myself; this is how I wish you to do.

Letter 271, to Sr. A. Augusta Biagini, L, May-June 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

In truth I never gained so much confidence with my Superior as when he rebuked me and reproved me for my faults.

* * *

We must teach humility and docility to people in the world, with good manners, full of divine unction.

cf. Letter 217, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 10 March 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Pride is abhorred by Jesus; so whoever is proud can expect nothing else but eternal death.

Letter 259, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Foligno, 9 May 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

In Heaven I will be content to be the footstool of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

Letter 377, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 5 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Do not grow proud on reading your mother’s letter because of the praises she gives you: if we have anything good, it is from God; we have nothing but misery and sins… Away with the world and its illusions; one thing alone remains for eternity: the good we will be able to do in this life with the help of God the Father; all the rest comes to be consumed with the earth, and remains lost in the dust, among the worms. Humility! for we have not yet learnt it!

* * *

Pride seems to sprout in our breast; and it stays there like a worm that is ever gnawing; blessed are those souls who knew how to drive this creature from its nest! Meanwhile there is always toil left in keeping on guard, so that it may not build its nest again, for it is always prowling about, and its intention and its labour is to be able to reach its goal. Alas! what can we do but watch, as our Master Jesus teaches us? “Watch and pray, that you may not fall into temptation”. Let us do so, then.

* * *

Humility is the foundation of every virtue: whoever has it possesses God.

Letter 97, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Genova, 10 June 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

My dear daughter, learn the beautiful practice of humility, and you will have everything from the Lord; your house will be a gem in the eyes of my Crucified One, and you will be its “beloved”. Courage, then, for violence is needed to acquire the treasures of Heaven.

cf. Letter 97, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Genova, 10 June 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Daughters, be strong, observant, docile, not proud; pride is the ruin of all the good of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

cf. Letter 122, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Piacenza, 20 August 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

She who keeps herself humble is sure to persevere; otherwise it is difficult to attain eternal life.

Letter 122, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Piacenza, 20 August 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Oh! humility, you are my fair one and my beloved!

Letter 322, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Rome, 5 April 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Daughters, I recommend humility to you; if you treat her well, this beloved of mine, you will see that you will draw from her an immense treasure. Yes, love her and treat her well: humility with everyone; the Inspector comes, humility; the Mayor comes, humility; treat everyone, everyone, to this exquisite dish, and you will see that they will be satisfied, and once they have tasted it you will become their favourites; even lions are caught with this net!… If I have had the good fortune to make some catch, I have always made it with the net of humility. So, my Daughters, let humility be a true comfort to you; and join with me in saying to her: “You are a treasure of love; all pure as gold, shining like a diamond”. With this enchanting balm you will obtain everything.

cf. Letter 322, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Rome, 5 April 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Daughters, great humility with everyone; this is the true means of triumphing over the wiles of the devil.

Letter 326, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Rome, 10 April 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

My Daughter, you tell me that you fear yourself: it is good to be always distrustful of ourselves, so as to be wholly Jesus’; so be at peace.

cf. Letter 186, to Sr. A. Guglielma Merli, Piacenza, 22 November 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

We must strive to cast down our self-love, a ferocious beast that gnaws away all the provisions which — with difficulty — we are gathering for the bundle of eternal life.

Letter 282, to Sr. A. Letizia Sordi, Piacenza, 14 April 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

Dearest Daughters, humility, the sure and only foundation for our sanctification; without it we can hope to have nothing for eternal life. It is written: if you wish to enter up there, you must make yourself little and humble. The Lord said to a soul: “Do not care for yourself, but only place your trust in me, and you will have everything”. So think of being wholly Jesus’, for Jesus always thinks of giving you what you need. Oh! blessed are you if He gives you His love!… certainly this cannot be had without humility.

Letter 291, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 3 May 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

All the good that we have is from God; from us comes misery, and nothing else.

Letter 334, to Sr. A. Veneranda Picco, Piacenza, 7 July 1879 — vol. 5

JESUS said to His Apostles, when they wanted the children to be sent away from Him: “Let the little children come to me”. What does this mean? That all those who go to Jesus stripped of every will of their own, and are not over-subtle in their doing, believing themselves able to discern, but who truly run to the Master to learn everything, and with the simplicity of little children, those will find on His bosom a place to rest.

cf. Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Live on your guard, for charity’s sake, live on your guard, so that the wolves, which alas are near, may not bite you. For this I pray every day, and I hope that God will hear me.

cf. Letter 16, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 June 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us rejoice in God, and thank Him for my recovered health; I am wonderfully well and always cheerful. My residence, day and night, is in the infirmary. Let all the Daughters be cheerful, as their “mother” is.

cf. Letter 6, to Caterina Rapallino, Cento, 5 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Jesus, beloved of sincere and good souls, You who are truth and life, You who love whoever bears the truth on her lips, grant that my Daughter may be a true dove, and Your (imitator) in speaking.

cf. Letter 114, to Carolina Pezzoni, Piacenza, 6 April 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

My Daughter, for charity’s sake, trample on human respect. Look, I will teach you what you must do when you see certain good souls who nevertheless fail in certain duties of piety; this is how it is done: at once we try to occupy our mind with this thought: “They, poor things, do not think of it; I will do it, and so the memory of having forgotten this or that act will be awakened in them”.

cf. Letter 114, to Carolina Pezzoni, Piacenza, 6 April 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

So in everything, my dear, try to do what this wretched one teaches you.

Letter 114, to Carolina Pezzoni, Piacenza, 6 April 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear Daughters of Saint Anne, God bless you; and may truth be kept on your lips, and likewise simplicity in your heart.

Letter 117, to the Sisters of the Community of Sampierdarena, Piacenza, 12 April 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Always remember these words, Daughter: “Let Truth be your treasure always”.

Letter 116, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 April 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

I must recommend to you that, both in your minds and among yourselves, you try to keep that holy evenness of affection which gives peace; moreover, when something happens concerning the House, let all try to keep silence and not to be upset; but to bring everything calmly to the feet of Jesus Crucified. He will set everything right, and will give you peace and comfort in the adversities of this wretched life.

Letter 128, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 6 June 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Each individual is master of his own actions. For charity’s sake, keep well in mind what this poor Mother of yours tells you: never tell lies, but let the truth always be on your lips, and you will live safe in the heart of Saint Anne our Mother.

Letter 133, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 2 July 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear Daughter, love the Eternal Father very much, flee often to Him and ask Him to tell you how you must conduct yourself; yes, this is how you must speak to Him; and every time you have to go to the door, first go into the Church and say to the Eternal Father: “My Father, tell me what I must say?… what must I answer?… take my tongue and exchange it for Yours, keep mine…” so your words will be exact and full of wisdom.

Letter 141, to Carolina Pezzoni, Genova, 22 August 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

When the confessor has these qualities, being reserved in speech and modest in bearing, that is enough to say that, if temptations sometimes arise, they are entirely the work of the devil. Forward, courage, without fear.

cf. Letter 151, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 October 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

This is the way in which we must converse, speak and make our confession: keeping our mind always in God; and then nothing will be able to enter it that is not of God.

cf. Letter 152, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 6 October 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

My dear daughter, for charity’s sake, do not let yourself be taken by whims or vague ideas, all things that muddle the mind, and serve for nothing else but to disturb us and make us irritable. Let us keep to what is solid, and let us take great care always to reason with the Crucified One before us, not at our side1; and let us look at Him in all our actions, to see whether they are in keeping with His example. And then everything is brought to nothing, and our sufferings become a mere nothing, and less than nothing.

cf. Letter 180, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 16 January 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, one does what one can, and the rest is left to God.

cf. Letter 68, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughter, keep fifty eyes on your (religious) Family, and in particular on the young girls.

* * *

As for (the Superior) going to the sick, I would be of the opinion that she should not, because it is good that the Superior should always remain at home for the good running of the house; and when the assistance cannot be given, it is left aside, unless it were a desperate case.

cf. Letter 49, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 1 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

When one does what one can, God is at once content; so let us do everything with holy simplicity; let us love God much, and seek to have everything from Him.

cf. Letter 68, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Do well to see that no one knows anything of your affairs. Silence with the confessors: they must know your sins and nothing more; keep hammering this point into your (religious) “daughters”, always, because it is never enough. If they do this, I assure you that peace and love will reign, and God will bless you and pour true providence upon you, and it will become a great and well-founded house.

Letter 100, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 19 September 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

All the posts of Superior carry the same weight in all the houses and in all the cities; the responsibility of that post admits of no exception.

Letter 111, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 15 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Whatever is given to you, take care to keep it well guarded, do you understand me?… You will say: “today the Mother is using a curious expression!” But this (expression) you must not take in its material sense, but rather…

Letter 131, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Genova, 7 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

You must never mention to the confessor the affairs of your “religious house”. And if you have anything to complain of, write it to the Superiors; but to the Confessor it belongs to tell your sins alone.

cf. Letter 139, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 29 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Where is the love you bear your Institute (of which, as you say, you desire nothing but the honour)? where is its glory, when instead you try to put it out in the street and to let everyone know your disorders, all of them arising from your sharp tongue, from your bad conduct and from your continual failures to observe your Rules? Consider that you are forcing the Superiors to use the whip to keep the “flock” of Saint Anne clean.

cf. Letter 139, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 29 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Among consolations there must also be bitterness, otherwise I would fear that it was not the work of God.

Letter 141, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 2 December 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

The Holy Mother wants observance: a member that does not stay subject to the body must be cut off.

Letter 141, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 2 December 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Superior, I recommend you to be very shrewd: do not trust appearances, because when a person is scheming, that is precisely when she seems good and full of zeal in her outward actions… Allow me to express myself in this way, since you are still a novice in the wiles of the world.

Letter 149, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 2 January 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

It is a grave fault to make remarks about the Superior’s command; and if such a fault is committed in public, penance must be done for it (in public), asking forgiveness for the scandal given.

* * *

The tongue that has been soiled with the sin of murmuring is no longer worthy that Jesus (hidden in the Host) should be placed upon it.

* * *

Superior, you are to tell all the Sisters to pray, and not to pay heed to gossip, not to answer, and so no one will know anything; among yourselves, be cheerful.

Letter 187, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 9 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

When it comes to listening, all are friends; but meanwhile they then make use of it for whatever suits them best.

Letter 191, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Every day God gives us occasion to watch over ourselves.

Letter 249, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 5 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Listen, Superior, a sure method for acting well (when remarks are made about the good running of the house): you must listen to everything, and then answer only this: “very well, I will think about it”. Then you must examine everything with patience and attention, commending yourself to God the Father, that He may provide you with the light needed in such a situation. What you see to be good and sensible you will put into effect, you will set things in order with firmness, and you will try to make it firm; the rest you will set aside and give it no weight.

cf. Letter 272, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 7 July 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

When I have to pronounce this name, “self-love”, I feel myself go all numb, particularly when I know that I am speaking with the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, and I think to myself: “can it be that this wicked thing (self-love) has been able to gain entry into this charitable family?”.

Letter 272, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 7 July 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

One must confess not the sins of the Community, but one’s own.

cf. Letter 294, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 6 September 18721 — vol. 2

* * *

In certain cases, dear daughter, you must decide for yourself: first commend yourself to God, and then forward with courage.

Letter 288, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 27 August 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Be ever more observant of your holy Rules, and in particular of the chapter (which deals with) never receiving alone persons of the other sex, neither priests nor laymen, nor anyone whatsoever; if you are faithful to this rule, I assure you that the Holy Mother will assist you and give you heart to observe all the others.

Letter 137, to Sr. A. del S. Cuore Cocchella, Piacenza, 24 October 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

The Superior must be all eyes, and must always turn as the yarn-winder does, so that nothing may escape her that she has not seen.

Letter 137, to Sr. A. del S. Cuore Cocchella, Piacenza, 24 October 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Dear Superior, my dear daughter, pay attention: I wish that in the evening, when the Rosary is over, you go straight to bed, and that the sisters be well persuaded that you go; that you be the first at meditation and at all the exercises of piety. Take good care not to make distinctions; not to tell the sisters that you know their faults because you read their hearts; not to make them deny their will too much, lest they lose their vocation; in these matters one must leave things to the Superiors. You must not call the sisters and require them to come every day to see whether or not they may make their Communion the next day; they must ask you for it only once a week.

cf. Letter 327, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Genova, 2 December 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Do not forget to remain always in the presence of God.

Letter 328, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 3 December 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

As regards the good soul whom you wish to visit, I would say that you should go, but with respect and without being curious in the least and seeking nothing; if she tells you something, believe everything, and make nothing of anything; do not dwell on it, leave everything in the hands of God: to Him everything and to us nothing, only confusion and meanness.

Letter 205, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Remember that the Superior is the yarn-winder of the house: she must turn continually and penetrate into every part so as to be able to see and to catch unawares, and if she could, she ought even to manage to see into hearts, so as with good manners to turn the Daughters away from every evil inclination and bring them back to the right path of holiness and perfection, and one day have them with her in Paradise for an eternity of joys.

cf. Letter 205, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Be prudent in speaking.

* * *

If you let yourself be taken by sadness, you will certainly do nothing good.

Letter 155, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 20 November 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Be simple, Daughters, for thus you will always have the white plumage of the dove, and the black feathers of the crow will never be able to grow in you.

Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and the Sisters of the Community, Genova, 25 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The devil is the enemy of our good works; he would like to divert us, so that we may then give way to his desires, which are those of perdition, and lead us with him to an eternity of torments. Be watchful.

Letter 193, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 13 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

How right is the point of our Rules about never being alone; for pity’s sake, never fail in this, and you will be glad of it.

Letter 199, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 22-23 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Do not be troubled, whether for little or for much; we are not infallible, but rather wretched human creatures, who, if good God did not uphold us with His right hand, would sink into the abyss of our iniquities.

Letter 200, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 23 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Let the “Daughters of Saint Anne” not have the vice of chattering with outsiders.

cf. Letter 408, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 30 October 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

It is my wish that the bread be good; since “providence” is there, let them (the Sisters) take care not to let themselves lack anything; waste, no, against the dear gem of poverty, no; but little and poor food, not that either, for they have much toil.

Letter 249, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 20 April 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

The devil is cunning: where one thinks he is sleeping, he is awake, and perhaps he is stealing.

Letter 278, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 6 June 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

When a certain person you know comes to bring messages, you, dear daughter, be sparing in speaking and in answering. If he speaks to you of money, never complain. If he should tell you to do this and that, you will answer: “I cannot do anything more than what my Superiors order me; we are daughters of obedience; let them write to the Mother and she will tell me what I must do”; and cut it short, for charity’s sake.

cf. Letter 319, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Nizza, 11 September 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Take care to be serious with people from outside.

* * *

Be always the same with everyone; cheerful, yes, but not with outsiders; do not go to eat in the houses of lay people, because it is against our Rules.

cf. Letter 122, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Piacenza, 20 August 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

I recommend you not to do things that would set people talking; everyone has their eyes on you: so edify your neighbour, do not give him scandal.

* * *

Prudence, yes, but not a prudence like that of the present day, by which, to do a little charity, we religious must be paid “to the rooftop”; how horrible!… an ugly spirit; our Saint (Saint Anne), who is full of charity, does not like it… she abhors it.

Letter 234, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Rome, 26 March 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Ah, for pity’s sake, Daughters, do not lose yourselves with lay people! I recommend you to live as true Religious, and to be observant: this will depend on your seriousness and your conduct; God wills it for the honour of His Institute, for pity’s sake. Daughters, you know that everything depends on you: remember that the world is watching you, and Jesus wants you to be mirrors. The example of virtue and wisdom that a Religious must give is never too much.

Letter 250, to Sr. A. Gesuina Moroni, Piacenza, 10 November 1876 — vol. 4

* * *

What the Superiors say must not be repeated, and complaining is one of the gravest sins.

cf. Letter 280, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Rome, 8 January 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Moderation is needed in everything: be moderate and you will last.

Letter 296, to Sr. A. Gesuina Moroni, Rome, 2 February 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Daughters, do not practise exaggerated economies, so as to take away what is necessary from yourselves and from others. Give up such an ugly way of proceeding and have meat, milk and wine bought, in the quantity and quality required by a Community of active persons such as you are.

cf. Letter 334, to Sr. A. Predicanda Romano, Napoli, 29 April 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Daughters, be cheerful, but always holily serious with men: never alone, never letting yourselves appear too bold.

* * *

Oh, how the world treats us!… its protection soon comes to an end. Only Jesus — who is “constancy” — remains to us: He is our sure pledge of eternal life; all the rest is deceitful and perishable. Men are like weathercocks in the wind, which turn wherever it blows strongest. Virtue alone is what can face every storm, because it alone becomes shield and defence, truth and perseverance in running the way of holiness.

Letter 169, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 25 October 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

I hold to this system: to set prayer and observance against our enemies.

Letter 174, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 7 November 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

My Daughter, every time you have to speak, never think — with too much anxiety — about what you must answer, wishing to use your own wit; no, no, present yourself to anyone whatsoever without study, save that of charity and gentleness, without affectation and with simplicity, always united to God, in His presence; and then speak without fear, for you will say everything well. Oh! sweet Jesus, whoever loves You knows how to speak well! So, dear daughter, love, and then do what you will, and you will do everything well.

cf. Letter 188, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 24 November 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Live in peace, Daughters. Quarrels in Communities arise when the sisters are not all treated equally; so everything depends on the Superior.

* * *

Daughters, promise to be good and never to fall into that ugly sin of murmuring, which is all the graver when it is done with lay people, because scandal is joined to it.

Letter 224, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli and Sisters, Napoli, 4 January 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

We must look upon the “confessor” as our Jesus, without thinking who he is.

Letter 371, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 10 September 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

My dear daughter Superior, if you are not attentive to the exercises of piety, your Community will go to ruin. Whoever lives distracted is soon lost, especially a Sister who is always sunk in the cares of the world: if she does not think of recollecting herself in God, she soon comes to a bad end! If a Superior is not very attentive that her subjects be observant, alas, what happens!… Everything lies in knowing how to cultivate them: they are plants which, if they have no manure, wither; and we must try to water them with healthful water, the water of which our Master Jesus spoke to the Samaritan woman; so a Superior must try to do everything so that her Sisters may have their fill of drinking this water; therefore meditation well performed, and the prayers in church likewise; gather them together frequently, and give them fine exhortations; do not allow them to converse with lay people, especially when they are ill; and the Superior must — as far as she can — be among them, otherwise someone who takes her place.

cf. Letter 377, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 18 September 1879 — vol. 5

BELOVED Daughter, God bless you and arm you with patience; may the mantle of our Holy Mother cover you, to hide you from the eyes of the world, so that you may not be stolen from Jesus, your Bridegroom.

Letter 44, to Caterina Rapallino, Genova, 26 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

My dear daughters, to attain the glory of Heaven, the happiness of seeing Jesus face to face, nothing else is needed but to despise, to despise everything that belongs to the world, and to see everything in Jesus, and to live for Jesus.

cf. Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

My dear daughter, when will that day come when you will be a true Daughter of Saint Anne, of our great Mother? A Daughter of this Great Woman thinks of nothing but serving her in the office and in the place where Jesus has put her, and has affection for no thing and for no person.

cf. Letter 36, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 28–30 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage, my Daughter, show yourself a generous Daughter of our Mother Saint Anne: a Daughter detached from everything, a Daughter who seeks nothing but the interest, the pleasure and the glory of God and of the great Saint Anne, who can accept as Daughters only those who show a generous heart, and who, for love of Jesus and for love of her, are ready to stay anywhere and to suffer every pain. Hold these words dear as though spoken by Saint Anne herself.

cf. Letter 36, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 28–30 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Strip yourself of the flesh and cast yourself into the Heart of Jesus, that He may clothe you with spirit alone; cast yourself into the Heart of Jesus, that He may purify you, and that in It you may die.

Letter 82, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, October 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

My Daughter, look at Jesus (in the crib): He has no clothes; so, to go freely to Him and to have His riches, we must be stripped of everything, poor and naked, and He will clothe us with beautiful garments adorned with precious gems.

cf. Letter 94, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

It is true that detachment from everything and complete stripping are things contrary and distasteful to our human nature, because it feels itself reduced to nothing in its sensible enjoyment; but the soul becomes more beautiful, and tastes the sweetnesses which Jesus lavishes on His true Brides.

* * *

In a few days the dear Little Child is coming, and He wants to find hearts empty, because He ardently desires to enter and rest. And should we refuse to give Him our heart? Ah! our heart is nothing in comparison with the Being who comes to dwell in it.

cf. Letter 95, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 23 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, tell me, does your heart not yet have a single beat for your beloved and beautiful Jesus?… do your eyes not gaze on Him Crucified? Who reduced Him to such a state, do you know?… our wickedness. Have you never looked at His beautiful mouth, how it is covered with blood?… His tongue parched with thirst?… His palate dried up? And this, why was He brought to suffer such torment? To atone for our greed and gluttony, in these days when nothing but sins are committed.

Letter 194, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 28 February at 11.30, 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear Jesus, in these days Your torments and sorrows are renewed! And even from one of Your Brides I see it suggested, so curtly, to depart from that small abstinence which Saint Anne placed in the “Rules” of her Daughters: to deprive oneself of eating meat dishes on the last two days of this diabolical worldly revelry (Carnival), so as to make reparation by this small abstinence for some least sorrow.

cf. Letter 194, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 28 February at 11.30, 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

I hope, dear daughter, that there you will have kept “abstinence” on the last two days of Carnival, and I would be greatly astonished if, merely with your permission, the poor Community had departed from it.

cf. Letter 194, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 28 February at 11.30, 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us look a little, my daughters, at where your mortifications of disordered sense are, the abstinences from all that our Rule forbids us. Ah! these mortifications our dear Jesus wants from our soul, because they alone are what will lead us to eternal life.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 9 March 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

We must always leave every taste of our own in order to serve God.

Letter 14, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

God alone is our all.

* * *

The Holy Mother will be deeply grieved to have Daughters so little mortified.

cf. Letter 85, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 4 August 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Ah! whoever is not mortified cannot be a good Christian… Gluttony is a monster that lowers our perverse nature to the ugliest actions.

Letter 85, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 4 August 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Ah! my dear daughter, for pity’s sake, do not attach your heart to the praises of this world, but consider that they are the plague of our soul. Flee, for pity’s sake, every thought that may have lodged in you; and say to your Jesus: “Our Good, drive far from me these diabolical firebrands, for I fear they may burn my soul; You alone, and nothing more”.

cf. Letter 149, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 2 January 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

God is everything for us, and for Him alone we labour.

Letter 264, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Ferrara, 15 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

How horrible! must the “Daughters of Saint Anne” die with the sin of intemperance in eating?… From now on I will no longer be indulgent, but as severe and austere as ever can be; at least on my part, at the tribunal of God I will have nothing that can condemn me. I think I give the example: they see these four bones… sick;… journeys, sufferings, torments;… a potato in water, a soup the same… and I find in it all the tastes in the world.

Letter 310, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Nizza, 5 October 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

God wills that, after having done so much and always worked under the whip, we should remain without ever a word of comfort. Behold, behold the wages of the world: let us glory in it, for we want our reward from Heaven, not from the earth or from all that it contains, since it is perishable stuff: but the kingdom of Heaven suffers no decay.

Letter 100, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 30 May 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Try to detach yourself from all earthly affections, from attachments to possessions and to the world, and to live for God alone; thus you will be a true Daughter of Saint Anne.

cf. Letter 131, to Maddalena Carmeli, end of September 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

All that belongs to this earth is dust and smoke.

Letter 15, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 10 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

When (in meditation) we are with Jesus in the desert, and we see Him all trembling with cold, with His feet bare and His head aching, and without a pillow on which to rest it,… that fair wavy hair, which appears so beautiful to our eyes and draws the gaze of the whole world,… how can we bear it?… Alas! my dear love! how can I bear to see You lie down and lay Your Head upon a stone? Ah no! let my head, I pray, serve You as a pillow; but what?… perhaps, because of the smoke of so many of my disordered appetites of the intellect, being full of pride, of self-love, of vainglory, all this will serve You for nothing else but to make You feel beforehand the sorrowful piercings. What am I to do, my Good?

cf. Letter 16, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 17 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Ah! Daughters, let us empty these faculties of ours of every earthly and perishing affection, so that Jesus may not disdain to come and lay His Head upon ours, and may accept it and rest upon it, and fill it with knowledge and with every virtue, and in particular with His continual presence.

cf. Letter 16, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, 17 February 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

I hope that I will soon see my dear daughters stripped of themselves, and all clothed by Jesus with charity, with patience, with confidence in God, with courage and with faith.

* * *

Have pity on your soul, which you keep shut up in the prison of your body: it weeps, because it is in the house of its Bridegroom and cannot even enjoy Him and taste His delights, because you continually let it die, that is, languish from hunger for good works and mortifications.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and the Sisters of the Community, Genova, 25 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The first mortifications are those of the tongue, then those of the thoughts, by driving them away, and above all when they concern the Superiors; other (thoughts) are those of gluttony; others, those desires for worldly happiness which often pass (through your mind); others are making little account of your vocation and of the great grace God has given you. Ah! Daughters, you who see so short a distance, try to see far, and then your gaze will be on high, never on the low things of the earth.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and the Sisters of the Community, Genova, 25 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Forward always with courage, and clinging to Jesus, held close to Him; for Him to live, for Him to die.

Letter 395, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 31 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Nowadays charity is dead, especially (among some) religious, and they keep this most precious gem under their feet, and know how to do nothing else but reckon up eating well. Ah, could I but once see them all filled with this eating up to their eyes! My dear daughter, forgive me this outburst, but when I hear this revolting “eating” in the mouths of religious men (and religious women), my nerves are set on fire and I can no longer contain myself; it truly harms my health. Ah! Jesus, who went into the desert and drew the crowds after Him, never thought that there was nothing to eat there, but rather thought of feeding their souls. And He?… what did He have? what did they give Him?… why did He not think of His apostles, who were poor? what was their future?… the Providence of God! Oh, dear Good, I have given food, I have distributed Your word, in short everything on the wings of Providence!

cf. Letter 395, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 31 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Death seals everything; with it every pain ends, and there remains in us the sweet thought of bringing our suffering to the Feet of Jesus in atonement for our sins, and the hope of being able to enter His Kingdom without having to wait in the antechamber (having waited so much in this world in the antechambers of the great, where one suffered cold and shame)! “Antechambers” are painful, and all too grievous would be that of not being able to enter soon to embrace Him whom one loves so much.

cf. Letter 375, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 2 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

When we have given ourselves to the Lord, He no longer wants us to have dealings with earthly things, but wants us to raise our mind to Him alone: He becomes jealous!

cf. Letter 300, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Rome, 8 February 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

My dear daughter, you ask me to do mortifications: I can permit nothing, because I am convinced that one thing alone can make Paradise sure for you, and that is the observance of the holy Rules and the life of perfect community. Yes, my dear Daughter, take care of yourself, and consider that for the glory of God we must toil.

Letter 204, to Sr. A. Letizia Sordi, Piacenza, 10 December 1878 — vol. 5

OH! come, my Daughters, let us cast far from us our swaddling bands, and then let us throw ourselves into the bosom of the Eternal One, and beseech Him to do with us what He wills. Yes, dear ones of Jesus, courage and constancy, and you will experience the help of God. To want to put in our own cooperation is a means of driving the divine workings away from us.

cf. Letter 7, to the Sisters of Piacenza, Cento, 18 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Steadfast, patience, endurance and courage: I am here for Jesus, and you too are in that house for Him!

* * *

You ask me, dear daughter, what you must do? I answer you that you know well that that is the “house” of penance and sacrifices.

cf. Letter 15, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 13 June 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Steadfast, dear daughter, patience and resignation: your “mother” labours for Jesus, and so does the daughter!

cf. Letter 8, to Giovanna Bixio, Cento, 20 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

It seems that that ugly monster (the devil) studies day and night how to make us despair. My dear Daughter, for charity’s sake, now is the most precious moment to give the Lord proofs of your love, and to bear witness to Him, by deed, that your life, your body, your soul are for Him. Ah! for charity’s sake, do not let yourself be overcome; and hold these words of mine as dictated by the heart of one whom you know well, who does not know how to pretend and who wants nothing but your good, that good which has no end and which must give you that All which no human creature can give you, but can only make you lose.

cf. Letter 87, to Caterina Rapallino, Cento, 4 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Blessed be that hand which deigns to strike us! I am in the midst of the most terrible battles: God alone can give us victory; our only weapon, our only shield of defence, is prayer. It is truly the time of the devil’s “great carnival”; but this must console us, because thus we are sure that as long as he makes efforts and battles to cast us down, it means that he is still angry and has nothing but defeats, so that, as far as we are concerned, he must be quite disheartened.

cf. Letter 88, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Cento, 5 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughter, remember to kiss that blessed Hand of God which strikes you, and then you will bear everything with resignation.

cf. Letter 92, to Caterina Rapallino, Piacenza, 16 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Courage, courage always, to fight well against the sad powers of the senses and of the flesh, and to will, at any cost, that the spirit may always be victorious in us.

Letter 94, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Let us trust in God, and He, since the Work is His, will provide for everything.

* * *

Daughter, on Tabor one may stay only to take a little refreshment; and Jesus wishes to bring weak souls there, for if He does not refresh them they die along the way; but the strong go ever onward… until they have reached Golgotha, and there the Crucifixion with Him, to rise again all beautiful, luminous, and to enter triumphant into the glory of Heaven.

cf. Letter 239, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, I desire that you be strong and all confidence in God.

Letter 41, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 5 April 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughters, courage, for the moment of trial is needed; courage, patience, peace, resignation: with these virtues everything is obtained, and every obstacle is overcome.

cf. Letter 69, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Rome, 11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

When I see that you do and act according as God inspires you, I feel immense consolation. Courage: it is in the fight that we must grow strong.

cf. Letter 72, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Rome, 16 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Let us work, for afterwards we will rest in blessedness. Stand firm, Daughter, do not fear; this poor mother of yours will always be at your side, wherever you go; you, take care to keep yourself in the presence of God, and you will see that you will have everything.

cf. Letter 90, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 28 August 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

One must never let oneself be overcome by faint-heartedness.

cf. Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Courage, for to die upon the Cross one needs strength and resignation. I have no rest, neither by day nor by night: always at the table writing from morning till evening; thoughts upon thoughts, labours upon labours; on every side I find cruel thorns, but always cheerful and always resigned: so Jesus teaches me.

Letter 191, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

It is time that you became strong women and nothing less; grow and be strengthened in the spirit of God, for this is the only thing we must desire and seek with unwearied zeal.

Letter 281, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 9 August 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Courage, (the Institute) is the work of God, so we must struggle with “cepinetto”.

Letter 281, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 9 August 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Be strong in the Work of God.

Letter 395, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 31 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Let the whole world talk: we do the will of God, and onward.

cf. Letter 107, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 11 June 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

My dear daughter, courage; the good God is greatly pleased with sacrifices. Ah! yes, for His Work one must go without sparing oneself, therefore… He gave all His Blood for us; and so must we do: yes! blood for blood!

Letter 135, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Piacenza, 19 October 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Courage and peace; thus we will overcome everything, and God, our eternal good, will give us the reward.

cf. Letter 40, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Sampierdarena, 3 April 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughter, do not fail to act courageously and firmly, without human respect.

Letter 189, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 4 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

In the battles that will arise let us pay no heed to anything; courage: until death we will cry out: “Long live Jesus”.

Letter 247, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Rome, 18 April 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Lies have short legs: this breed of sin soon comes to a halt, unable to go any further, and shows itself with its face uncovered. I greatly rejoice that the rusty pot is throwing out - in its boiling - the rusty iron. When (the consequences of the lies) are over, then we will begin to rejoice with the Lord over the beautiful and gracious persecutions they procure for us. Onward, courage, for they have not yet wounded you, because our breast is of bronze. Let us love God, and for Him let us suffer everything in His honour and glory.

cf. Letter 383, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, 14-16 December 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Whoever knows that she has God is powerful in everything: with Him the whole of hell is overcome.

cf. Letter 159, to Sr. A. Guglielma Merli, Piacenza, 21 October 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Dear daughters, be strong when it is a matter of defending the work of the Lord.

SPEAK little and pray much: you will be glad of it, not only on the day of judgement, but also now, because in silence the soul can converse with Jesus, and always finds her Bridegroom, and rejoices in His union.

Letter 117, to the Sisters of the Community of Sampierdarena, Piacenza, 12 April 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let the Daughters of Saint Anne take care to observe the mitigated silence (as well as the strict one), because Jesus dwells in silence and in recollection. Souls that live in distraction never taste God.

cf. Letter 147, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 September 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, if you wish to taste your “Bridegroom”, flee every noise, and strive to remain in silence: then you will converse with Him and taste Him fully.

cf. Letter 147, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 September 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Be firm in the observance of the Holy Rules and of the strict and mitigated silence.

cf. Letter 151, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 October 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

I had to feel a mortal wound when I was told that in that House you spoke so loudly… and in the time of “mitigated silence”. And today, towards the end of recreation, my mind was all upset by the thought: “what will become of those daughters now that it is recreation time?”

My God, I would have flown there to prevent such a scandal! What can you bring forward, in the Presence of God the Father, to excuse yourselves for this fault of yours? perhaps that you did not think of such a thing, not being accustomed to it?… no, no, because this Mother of yours has warned you a million times, exhorting you to this observance, giving you examples, making you know the harm that comes from this great fault.

Do penance, therefore, for this great fault, so as to appease the Eternal Father, by keeping “strict silence” for two days: and for the whole week let your recreation be “mute”; only when holding your nursing school, you will hold it entirely in “mitigated silence”. Thus you will be able, in part, to make amends for so much harm that you have done.

* * *

I recommend, dear daughters, the strict and mitigated silence, because without it there can be no order. Remember that you are religious by the grace of God.

cf. Letter 139, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 29 November 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Dear daughters, I will dip my pen in the sea of the most Divine Heart of Jesus, the most Holy Blood, so as to be able to touch well upon certain points of the Holy Rules which I found neglected. First, the mitigated silence: daughters, truly I tell you that these words of yours are so many wounds to the Heart of your Holy Mother Saint Anne; then that immoderate laughter in time of recreation…; remember that you are Religious, Brides of a Bridegroom who is all gentleness and courtesy, and rudeness does not please Him. Now I leave it to you to make an exact examination, and then to pray the Sacred Heart to open the cavern of His Side and keep you there, hidden within it by His mercy, so that in that Most Holy Heart you may learn most sublime lessons. There I embrace you all.

cf. Letter 232, to the Sisters of the Community of Sampierdarena, Piacenza, 15 June 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Without silence one cannot have a holy and good community; peace cannot exist; there will be nothing but intrigues, and there will be quarrels continually.

Letter 236, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 18 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Where there is much noise, nothing reigns but the devil. Jesus is where silence dwells; and it is then that He abides there; He speaks to hearts, inflames them, enlightens them: but whoever is always going about, and with her tongue in the air, certainly will never be able to have anything, and her salvation will always be in doubt.

Letter 236, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 18 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Peace, dear daughters, peace, silence, calm; then you will hear God, who will come to speak to your heart with loving and all-sweet words.

TO be admitted to make simple vows, one must practise true obedience to the Superior; it does not consist in “eating the virtue of a good soup”, but only in abandoning oneself to the will of the Superior.

cf. Letter 16, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 June 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Love one another, all with one heart, and love your Superior as Jesus, because you must see in her the figure of your Bridegroom. If He Himself were to command you, what perfect obedience would you not render? Well then, He commands you through your Superior.

cf. Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

May God bless you, and grant that you may always be ready to give your life for obedience, and so to merit Heaven.

* * *

The time of probation - in the novitiate - serves to see whether the Sisters know how to practise obedience, and not to see whether they do penance and whether they eat little, because in this, many times, I find caprice and not virtue…

* * *

We must work: holiness consists in obedience, and not in not eating. So I mean to speak to all; abstinences (without obedience) are of no use to you: ashes for hell. On the day of judgement you will see whether this creature was telling the truth!

cf. Letter 106, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5 February 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Obey, if you wish to be saints; and may God grant that I may soon see in you that holy, exact observance required by our Holy Rule. Yes, my dear daughters, be ready for everything, and if your Superior were to set you to wash the latrines for the whole of your life, believe that if you do it with a true spirit of obedience, I assure you that you will sanctify yourselves in this office too, like those who are in offices of greater importance and - in appearance - an easy road to holiness. Be sure that all sanctification lies in obedience.

Letter 123, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 4 May 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, if I had to pay heed to my body, it would certainly be rashness to undertake so long a journey, because, humanly speaking, I have no more hope of health; but if God so commands, I go, leaning upon His “providence”.

Letter 57, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 25 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

In the Conferences, make them feel the price of obedience; we can have no good if this is lacking to us, because whoever does not obey shows that she wishes to do her own will, not that of God, our only treasure: the Religious who does her own will is a shadow that walks about the Cloister without belonging to it.

Letter 277, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 26 July 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

A disobedience deserves a severe penance.

Letter 13, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 24 January 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

When obedience is done, everything turns out well, and it is most pleasing to God.

cf. Letter 139, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1–8 August 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

At times (certain) religious complain loudly that their Superior is too severe; I believe it is because it displeases them to remain in submission.

* * *

Obedience! This is the only virtue that we can have, and that we must have as our emblem.

Letter 429, to Sr. A. Santina Solenghi, Piacenza, December 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Nothing can be good that is contrary to the will of our Superiors.

cf. Letter 372, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 14 June 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

Dear daughters, let us obey blindly. Look, I am dying with the desire to go to America; but my Superiors said “no”; oh! I repeat: “no, no!”. If we want love, we must obey; let them call me ignorant, stupid, senseless… oh! blessed am I, if they give me these titles after I have obeyed.

Letter 129, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 19 August 1878 — vol. 5

I assure you that our poverty gives me concern: patience! Now I would not wish to dishearten you, having made you this confidence, but you will take it with patience and resignation, thanking the Lord who wishes to humble us in this way.

cf. Letter 28, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 14 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

We are so short of means that I do not know where my head is!… if you only knew! here, to shelter ourselves from the cold, we have managed as best we could with rags!… now see, I always hope in the mercy of the Lord, that He will not send cold, because I assure you it is a fine predicament!

Letter 37, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 3 October 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

How it grieves me to hear that you are cold! My Jesus, give my daughters Your fire and they will be sheltered! I am convinced that if you have great faith, first in our Eternal Father and then in Saint Anne, you will see that you will find everything you need.

Letter 163, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1 December 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Providence makes you sigh; do you know why?

Letter 64, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 6 June 1871 — vol. 2

My daughter, truly this mother of yours assures you that the higher the degree of confidence one has in God, the more provident His mercy becomes towards us, and from every side it pours out providence. Courage.

Letter 147, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 18 September 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, I am sorry that you have not yet been able to pay any bill; well then, the Holy Mother will pay them all, do not doubt, trust in God, and you will have everything.

Letter 233, to Sr. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 3 July 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Be cheerful with Jesus; yes, my daughter, when we have the Eternal God with us, what do we lack? nothing, nothing; we are truly rich, and we defy the whole world, belonging as we do to our Bridegroom.

cf. Letter 233, to Sr. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 3 July 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Pray for “Providence”: whoever prays well obtains everything.

Letter 36, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 23 March 1871 — vol. 2

Here Saint Joseph worked truly great miracles for us, as great as He is in Heaven!

cf. Letter 36, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 23 March 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Courage and patience: the Lord will soon come with special providence;… I do not lack in the least trust in God the Father. He will provide when we least think of it. Let us pray with fervour, so that our prayers may reach the Loving Heart of Jesus: it is there that the source of all riches, spiritual and temporal, is found.

cf. Letter 341, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Genova, 30 December 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

My blessed daughters, stand firm and all confidence in God; embrace, love your privations, the discomfort that your human nature must bear; treasure these riches, and with gladness offer them to your Eternal Father, that He may deign to accept them and keep them, changing them into some little treasure of His own.

Letter 54, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 22 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

What delight, dear daughters, to think that for so little suffering (poverty and privations) you will have great joy; and your heart will feel beforehand the joy of the love of its Beloved, and you will come to experience immense contentment from it; and may God grant that you may taste this honey of suffering, which is the essence of every good.

Letter 54, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Piacenza, 22 May 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Do you know why Providence makes you sigh? Because it wants us to pray ever more: our dear Jesus delights in seeing Himself prayed to.

cf. Letter 64, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 6 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Make a novena to Saint Joseph and say to him: “Hear us, dear support of the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate”, and you will see that Providence will come. But do not harass the saints: pray to them with patience and resignation.

Letter 68, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Courage (in poverty), because your tribulations are few in comparison with those of the House of Nazareth, which was lacking in everything, and within it dwelt the three richest personages of Heaven: there was no bed, but only straw in the hut of Bethlehem! and yet the Son of God chose it for His first dwelling and willed to be born there. The Queen of Heaven seated where? on the straw and beside a manger, feeding only on the beautiful light of Jesus; in Him she found everything: the comforts, the delights of the world; in that dear Little Child she held everything enclosed. And you, who can gaze upon Him within your heart, behold, you will find every delight if you keep your gaze on Him alone. May God be ever blessed, who deigns to lower His Most Holy Hand. Be ever blessed in your tribulations.

cf. Letter 69, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Rome, 11 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Regarding poverty, you say you are ashamed? I do not understand this language: to be ashamed of what we make a vow of?… with God’s help, we must rather strive to put it into practice…! Who was poorer than Jesus? If we are to be imitators of Him, we must always be in stables, in caves. You are neither in caves nor in stables; and if they tell you that you are poor, (answer): “this is our treasure! And if we had the revenues of Croesus, our dwellings would still always be these, because so the vow we make requires of us… and we are so content”.

cf. Letter 76, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 24 June 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

The black “vita”2 that I left behind… was dearer to me, because it was patched.

* * *

What is Saint Joseph doing? is he bringing providence? cry out loudly, because he is old, and… one must shout! That is why he does not hear me, since I have little voice. Dear Saint, I hope greatly in this month of his!

cf. Letter 191, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

“Providence” will come, do not distress yourself, Daughter. God will think of us, if we think of Him alone. Have the novena for “Providence” to Saint Joseph repeated, and ask him to give you humility, and through this virtue to give you — in it, — Providence.

Letter 279, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 3 August 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

My dear daughters, you know well how dear poverty is to this Mother of yours; she loves it, embraces it, always clasps it to her breast; but my soul is wounded by you on this account, because I perceive in you that you love it little and, to put it better, you do not know it. Listen, I find no phrases to make you know its exquisiteness; I will only tell you that it is the treasure of the Saints.

Letter 292, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 4 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

“Yes, we are poor and we rejoice in it”. Ah! if I heard this repeated to me by the “Daughters of Saint Anne”, I would be happy.

Letter 292, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 4 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Some daughters will have nothing to do with poverty: my God, what pain! Well then, the Holy Mother compels them to embrace it by force, making “providence” scarce.

cf. Letter 292, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 4 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Pray to obtain from God “providence” and together with it the gift of putting poverty into practice and loving it, and of feeling the relish of this treasure; and meanwhile promise Him that — with His divine help — you will practise it.

cf. Letter 292, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 4 September 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

O blessed poverty, my most beloved sister! love it you too, dear daughters.

* * *

When a Work is wholly God’s, “providence” certainly cannot be lacking.

* * *

The Holy Mother (Saint Anne) wants us to practise poverty, and, if she did otherwise, we would become an abyss of pride, worse than Lucifer.

cf. Letter 137, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, July 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Listen, when you write to me, take care not to leave so much paper blank, but write to me at the top of the page, as I do, because it is a fault against poverty.

Letter 350, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Piacenza, 3 November 1874 — vol. 3

TO be perfect Religious one must:

1st Obey blindly, when things against the Holy Rule are not commanded, because then, in this case, one has recourse calmly to whoever is needed, and with all charity one seeks to say how the matter stands.

cf. Letter 8, to Giovanna Bixio, Cento, 20 February 1867 — vol. 1

2nd Never make reflections on the manner of acting of the Superiors.

3rd Bear with holy resignation all the annoyances that are given us; have compassion on all: sisters, the sick, superiors, inferiors.

Letter 8, to Giovanna Bixio, Cento, 20 February 1867 — vol. 1

4th Keep one’s thought turned to God, and see everything in Him. And when one is in desolation, call often upon Jesus, Mary, Saint Anne.

cf. Letter 8, to Giovanna Bixio, Cento, 20 February 1867 — vol. 1

5th Do with all diligence what is commanded us, and carry out with perfection the office one holds, were it even the lowest.

Letter 8, to Giovanna Bixio, Cento, 20 February 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

You will tell the Daughters of Saint Anne to be composed in whatever office they find themselves; to be cheerful with moderation and not to laugh too much, especially when there are men present.

* * *

Here among us we enjoy a peace of Paradise; everything goes with perfect exactness, and so I hope it will be among all of you daughters there: you will love one another with one heart, and will always mirror yourselves in your Bridegroom Jesus, to see in Him the model according to which you must adorn yourselves, the model to imitate in order to practise that evangelical charity counselled and practised by our Redeemer, and dear and holy humility.
