cf. Letter 18, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 5–17 July 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Yes, dear daughters, if we wish to learn we must keep ourselves before the divine mirror, “Jesus”; we must always keep before our eyes the figure of the Redeemer, and gaze upon it continually, and then we will do everything with perfection.

* * *

We must strive to correspond to every inspiration that our dear Jesus never ceases to give us, and many times, perhaps, makes us feel strongly. Often we reject them with the greatest indifference, as if they were things of no account; and yet, for these, one day a great account will be asked of us; and woe to that creature who has made herself deaf to the inspirations that God, in His mercy, has given her.

Letter 94, to Sr. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 21 December 1868 — vol. 1

* * *

Let my daughters be silent; let them act in such a way as to win the hearts of the girls; let them be hard-working and good and observant of the holy Rules.

* * *

To become a nun one must thoroughly embrace all the sacrifices, which are: austerity of life, poor food, the perfect life of community, the care of the sick.

cf. Letter 127, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 4 June 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

May the Lord bless (the Daughters of Saint Anne) and make them great saints, but true saints. Let them take care to put into practice what I taught them regarding silence and (common) recreation, and if they do this, they will grow in spirit and in virtue; and moreover a true peace, a holy harmony will reign (in the Community), and all their actions will be in God.

cf. Letter 141, to Carolina Pezzoni, Genova, 22 August 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

The letter from the Rev. is two “malonnese” words on a sheet, and you say that their content is only insults?… Well then, are you perhaps not content that Jesus uses these ways with you? Seeing you still too weak to receive certain affronts face to face, He sends them to you in writing, so that you may practise! What a dear Bridegroom, how well He knows how to treat His beloved ones! with what means He goes graciously and little by little training them in perfection. Courage, Daughter, be all confidence in the good God, and if you do this, you will enjoy a Paradise in advance.

cf. Letter 154, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 15 October 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

The Lord is our help and our “master”, and He knows how to teach us well. Let us strive to profit from His lessons, and to be studious, so as to give Him pleasure and fully satisfy His will.

* * *

Here below we can have nothing good; only that joy which we procure for ourselves in acting for God alone.

Letter 111, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 15 October 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

One must strive always to preserve that bearing and composure, mingled with meekness and charity, which are the true portrait of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

Letter 150, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 8 January 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Courage, patience, resignation to the will of God; with this we will give good example.

Letter 233, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The Superiors are the shadow of the other religious: all run after it, and go as their shadow teaches them the way. If a mother is irascible, and always shouts, and always keeps a sad face, behold, all the children do the same, and order no longer reigns in that family: one shouts on one side, another screams on the other; in the end, the devil sleeps upon their roofs, having no more work to do, and because, little by little, behold, they end with grave offences against the Lord.

cf. Letter 233, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Patience, docility, resignation are those qualities which God requires a good Superior to have.

Letter 233, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Ferrara, 13 May 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The silence, the order, the good little girls, the work, everything gives me a sign that God is there; may His spirit reign in your heart. Work: ah! where there is no idleness there is certainly peace.

Letter 252, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Ferrara, 8 June 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

The observance of the timetable in the Community, the Rules, meditation and silence are those points on which the whole edifice of good order rests; when these are observed with exactness, you can be sure that all the others are observed.

Letter 277, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Piacenza, 26 July 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

How willingly one serves this dear Master, who is so gentle in commanding and is content with everything, provided that our actions are upright, and only for that end of pleasing Him and serving Him as He deserves!

cf. Letter 131, to Maddalena Carmeli, end of September 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Prudence, meekness and charity: with these three virtues, Daughter, you will guide the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, along the way of perfection.

cf. Letter 271, to Sr. A. Augusta Biagini L, May-June 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Tell me, dear daughters, why (when you receive a correction) do you make together all those foolish resolutions, whispering in one another’s ear, saying certain things that do your souls no good, being against perfection?… This way of acting makes you lose altogether the confidence of the Superiors, who stand in the place of God.

cf. Letter 197, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa and the Sisters of the Community, Genova, 25 March 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

May God give you strength to be able to do everything well for Him alone; we want nothing else.

cf. Letter 227, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 20 March 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

I recommend to Sister A. N. not to give poor food, because all, in general, complain of the kitchen of P… Let her know that she is cooking for the Servants of the Lord.

Letter 232, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Rome, 23 March 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

The spirit of the Institute must be on your face: courage, docility, love of God; to think always of Jesus, to strive to do everything in His presence, and in everything to strive to be humble, thinking that whatever good you do will have been done by our dear Master Jesus, who in His infinite goodness deigns to lower Himself and to do for us what we are incapable of doing, being such wretched creatures.

cf. Letter 348, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 3 November 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

I desire that your conversations be all holy, and so too your actions.

cf. Letter 362, to the Sisters of the Community of Ferrara, Piacenza, 19 November 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

I am glad to hear that my daughter asks God for help to be able to curb her passions; yes, He alone can help you. Think often that with these continual renewals of our resolutions we make ourselves dear to God;… oh, blessed that soul who will come to be a delight to her God!… a brief suffering for an eternal joy. Courage, then, and think often of what you have promised to God in your Superiors.

Letter 153, to Sr. A. Maddalena Terzaghi, Piacenza, 13 November 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Jesus wants generous souls! My God, bless my dear daughter, so that she may become an exemplar… and that from her mirror many models may be drawn, since your Work requires them; so it must be.

cf. Letter 249, to Sr. A. Guglielma Merli, Piacenza, 9 November 1876 — vol. 4

* * *

The days fly, and soon we will see each other again. Oh, what beautiful things will we not tell each other about the Work of the Lord! Courage, then, and love of God in all things; charity towards one’s neighbour, renunciation of oneself, and one will have what one desires.

cf. Letter 414, to Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, Piacenza, 19 November 1877 — vol. 4

* * *

If only we all worked in our little piece of ground that God has given us to cultivate, and formed in our heart a solitary dwelling, and thought of nothing else but loving and serving the good God!… and in the solitude of this inner chamber formed an altar to adore our Jesus alone!… Oh, then indeed all other things could not come to wound our ears, but instead we should always be intent on listening to His voice, which can be heard in solitude. Blessed are you, dear daughters, who can pass from work to the (inner) chamber in retreat.

Letter 21, to Sr. A. Maddalena Terzaghi, Rome, 3 February 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Therefore, suffering, suffering and love; ears closed and heart open; and in Him and for Him alone work and love.

cf. Letter 21, to Sr. A. Maddalena Terzaghi, Rome, 3 February 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Dear daughters, strive to do everything with order. Always be accompanied (when dealing with lay people), never alone;… yes, you must be the champion of the Institute, and, if you do well and bear fine fruit, everyone will want a branch of your tree; courage, then.

Letter 113, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 3 August 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Oh, dear daughters, let us do everything for the glory of God and for the good of our neighbour: let us see in those dear sick people the person of our Lord, our dear Redeemer! It is truly a sweet thought: to tend the wounds of Jesus!… blessed are you who can always have Him before your eyes and in your heart… Jesus in the bed of the sick… Jesus in all your offices! What infinite sweetness! Without Him there is nothing good or beautiful; with Him we have everything, we lack nothing; and to be sure of having Him with us, and of doing all that pleases Him, let us obey, and we will be sure of pleasing Him, and of having Him for an eternity.

cf. Letter 239, to Sr. A. Santina Solenghi, Rome, 19 January 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

Daughter, courage and strength; and always united to God; and strive to remain in His presence in all things, and so you will draw light from it to guide your little flock well.

cf. Letter 246, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Napoli, 30 January 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

Daughter, for charity’s sake, seek to edify, for so your mission will be acceptable to God.

DEAR daughters, live observant of your holy Rules and obedient, and you will surely have Paradise.

* * *

Daughter, do not be distressed, for the holy Mother will accept the desires you have to be exact in her holy Rules.

* * *

Saint Anne desires her daughters to be observant of the holy Rules, beginning in the morning, at the opening of their eyes, until the evening, when overcome by sleep.

cf. Letter 117, to the Sisters of the Community of Sampierdarena, Piacenza, 12 April 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Let your Rules be your treasure.

* * *

Remind yourselves often why you became Religious: to become saints. Therefore, if you desire this, read your Rules often, and strive to imprint them on your heart and mind so as to observe them exactly. God will help you to put them into practice, and by this means you will become saints.

cf. Letter 128, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 6 June 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Let the Daughters of Saint Anne strive to be observant of the holy Rules; otherwise the holy Mother herself will know how to punish and cleanse her flock.

* * *

Strive to be exact in the observance of the holy Rules, and then Jesus will be generous in dispensing His graces to you. He wants sacrifice, because there is no other means of drawing graces from His Heart but sacrifice.

cf. Letter 158, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 4 November 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, have you ever seen this poor Mother of yours deviate from the least of the holy Rules? Going over at once, with an exact examination, even the small observances, both of the timetable and of the Rules, I do not find that I have ever either permitted or omitted the least thing; and indeed I am and will be, with God’s help, most rigorous, and I will never make the least concession.

Letter 194, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 28 February at 11.30, 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

What consoles me most of all is the observance of your Rules and of the timetable. God will not fail to help you and make you prosper.

Letter 213, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 28 April 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, you ask me to teach you a little flower for the whole month in honour of Mary. What could be more pleasing to the Virgin than the little flower of the exact observance of the Rules and the fulfilment of our duty, of that employment in which our Jesus has placed us?

Letter 217, to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Sampierdarena, 4 May 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Dear daughters, for me the only consolation is to hear that you are truly observant of your holy Rules.

* * *

I recommend you to observe the timetable exactly, beginning with rising in the morning, until rest in the evening; if this is done, the blessing of the Lord will not be lacking in that house; otherwise everything falls back into ruin and God suspends divine providence.

cf. Letter 222, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Ferrara, 27 April 1872 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughter (Superior), spare nothing for the observance, and you will see that God will bless you. Thoughtless is that Superior who keeps silent about the faults of her daughters so that the Superiors may not know of them, and covers up their failings, keeping the Superiors in the dark.

cf. Letter 13, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Rome, 24 January 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

The devil is cooking up pots on every side; but if we pray and are observant, the devil certainly will be able to do nothing to us; and from the harm done to us the good God draws a great good.

cf. Letter 66, to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti, Rome, 20 March 1873 — vol. 3

* * *

Daughter (Superior), strive to have observed what I left said; firm in the observance of the holy Rules; firm in all that I left prescribed to be done, and you will see that you, my dear, will enjoy true peace in your house, and you will prosper, and Providence will never be lacking in all that you need.

cf. Letter 139, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 1–8 August 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter Superior, be cheerful: the Lord loves you; strive to correspond by the observance of the Rules and by having them observed by your sisters, those whom God has entrusted to you. You must see to it that they are always according to His Heart, good, docile and observant: this is what is needed to content the Heart of God.

Letter 217, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 10 March 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

My daughter, if you do not see to it that the observance of the holy Rule is maintained, all other things will go from bad to worse. Observance is the pivot of our actions, and without it we can do nothing good: laxity begins; harmony among the sisters vanishes; murmuring becomes the chief business of the day; worst of all, certain shameful things happen which are the ruin of Communities. Observance is the sweet bond of perfection, that which helps us, one with another, to run along that dear path of peace and union.

Letter 259, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Foligno, 9 May 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

For pity’s sake, let us put ourselves in order with the observance, because otherwise it is labouring in vain; and then everything will end with the end of our life. Let us build on solid ground, not on sand, so that our edifices may last for an eternity.

cf. Letter 259, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Foligno, 9 May 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

Observance is the anchor that holds us fast in the harbour of our vocation.

Letter 267, to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini, Rome, 14 February 1874 — vol. 3

* * *

May God bless all my dear “Daughters of Saint Anne”, above all the most observant: oh, for these, who are truly the consolation of the holy Mother, I feel a great affection, and I look upon them with delight, as my Mother Saint Anne looks upon them!

cf. Letter 53, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Piacenza, Genova, 1–5 March 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

I recommend, for pity’s sake, the observance and the timetable, and likewise the works of piety; when these diminish, all is lost, and nothing good remains any more, and the loss of the vocation is certain. Courage, then, everything for Jesus, life and soul, everything for Him.

Letter 98, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Piacenza, 30 June 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

When one observance is neglected, all the others behave like playing cards: they go and fall down on top of it.

cf. Letter 122, to Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, Piacenza, 20 August 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Daughter Superior, for charity’s sake, observance: the chapter every 15 days; the retreat, silence and the reading of the Rule, so that the sisters may learn it by heart and you may always be guided, by the holy words of our Rules, in all your steps and in all your actions; always at the prayers of the Community and at meditation. And I tell you that if you do what I counsel you, providence will never be lacking to you.

cf. Letter 140, to Sr. A. Felicita Grisleri, Piacenza, 18 October 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

The Lord will pour out His graces upon you, provided that you are observant of your holy Rules, and that the Community is at peace in His holy Name.

Letter 166, to Archbishop Mgr Eugenio Cecconi, Rome, 18-22 December 1875 — vol. 4

* * *

Courage, and firm in the Rules; a thousand deaths, but observant; and if you do this, be assured that you will be with me in Heaven for all eternity.

Letter 111, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 2 August 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

Observance is the only thing that serves to sanctify us.

cf. Letter 156, to Sr. A. Gesuina Moroni, Piacenza, 19 (8)1 October 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

We must study much to become observant, and so dear Jesus will give us a share in His love. Oh, dear Bridegroom, such is Your balm that it suffices to sweeten any pain. Love, love Him alone, for He alone can make you happy for an eternity.

Letter 282, to Sr. A. Letizia Sordi, Piacenza, 14 April 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

We have had the definitive approval of our Institute… I hope, Daughter, that you will have established the life of perfect community, and that you will no longer have to dine with anyone, whether priest or layman or friar. Alas! a relaxed “Body” (or Community) is dead to every grace. Do not let yourselves be deceived for any reason whatsoever. Now, moreover, that the Church has “approved” us, we are under strict obligation to observe our Rules to the letter, without human respect and with frankness. Courage, my daughter, for if one does not wage war, one does not win medals and positions. Soldiers aspire to earthly posts of honour, and we… other, better posts await us: those of Heaven. Oh, yes! whoever presents herself up there well furnished with medals for having fought and conquered, to her a crown will certainly be given and a most beautiful place, which has nothing to do with earthly miseries. Strong, then, like the lion, and do not compromise.

cf. Letter 291, to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni, Piacenza, 3 May 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

It is better to lose everything than to transgress a “rule”. We must be observant if we wish to please God and to be true Daughters of Saint Anne; better to die than to deviate; therefore, dear daughters, firm until death. Whoever perseveres is sure of eternal life.

cf. Letter 356, to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli, Piacenza, 18 August 1879 — vol. 5

* * *

Greatly will she console me who says to me: Mother… I will try to do honour to my dear Institute!… and for it I will give my whole life, and in dying I desire nothing else than to see myself consumed for it, and to be able to say that for the observance I have been brought to death! Courage, and victorious, yes, we will carry off the palm!

cf. Letter 404, to Sr. A. Del Buon Pastore Dosi, Piacenza, 27 October 1879 — vol. 5

DEAREST daughters, may the Immaculate be your consolation!

Letter 10, to Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 22 March 1867 — vol. 1

With most intense sorrow I heard that D. and E. are ill. The Lord wishes to humble us in everything. As for the doctor, I think we should turn, before anyone else, to the physician of all our sorrows: to our Mother Saint Anne; she will see to it that they recover.

cf. Letter 29, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 19 September 1867 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughters of Saint Anne, a Mother wholly ours, strive to merit being numbered among those who, with transports of love, will be able to say: The holy Mother is wholly ours. One thing alone can separate you and make you orphans: the transgression of your holy Rules, the non-observance of the timetable, lack of exactness, the poor fulfilment of your office, always wanting to observe the conduct of the Superiors, keeping everything to oneself. Believing themselves too good, some do not go to recreation, thinking it is made only for the distracted ones, and so the Rule is neglected, and so irregularities are committed. (I say to those who behave in this way): “Humble yourselves, proud ones, go to recreation, speak with your sisters who, like you, are truly angels; and all with one thought, with one heart, strive to encourage one another in the observance of your Rules, and in these you will acquire true virtue, and you will be able to say, and merit, to be”Daughters of Saint Anne” and say to her: “You are our Mother, wholly ours!”.

cf. Letter 142, to Carolina Pezzoni, Genova, 25 August 1869 — vol. 1

* * *

Mary, Mary!… Behold the Mother of sorrows! Who more beautiful than you among all peoples?… Yet you have suffered the anguish, the cruellest torments that a Mother’s heart could suffer! Now all the heavenly legions together do not come to form a part of your beautiful and most resplendent light: a single ray of yours suffices to illumine the whole of Heaven!

Letter 239, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

What do you think, daughter?… Is it better to rejoice, or is it better to suffer?… I leave the choice to you.

cf. Letter 239, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Answer me, and reflect whether it is true, as this poor Mother of yours tells you, that in suffering there lies a most delicious honey;… and learn to taste this fruit, and you will see that you will never have enough of it to be sated.

Letter 239, to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Piacenza, 12 August 1870 — vol. 1

* * *

Daughter, I hope to find you cheerful and wholly transformed into Saint Anne; her true disciple: her speech, her countenance, her gaze.

cf. Letter 22, to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, Sampierdarena, early March 1871 — vol. 2

* * *

Daughter, you must place your trust in God, in Saint Anne and in Most Holy Mary, and you will see that all will go well. We are capable of nothing without the help of God, and with it we have everything; courage and patience.

Letter 176, to Sr. A. Teodora Barisioni, Piacenza, 8 November 1878 — vol. 5

* * *

The Holy Mother will not allow you to suffer. She will always defend her daughters and will protect them through all the ages, until the end of the world, without their being molested in the least.
